claims.quote: is a demigod in the Hindu epic Rāmayana, who has the form of a vulture.

claims.statement: Jatayu is an old friend of Dasharatha, Rama's father.
claims.statement_id: Jatayu merupakan sahabat lama Dasharatha, ayah Rama.
claims.quote: Jatayu (Sanskrit: जटायु, IAST: Jaṭāyu) is a demigod in the Hindu epic Rāmayana, who has the form of a vulture. He was the younger son of Aruṇa and his wife Shyeni, the brother of Sampati, and the nephew of Garuda. He was also an old friend of King Dasharatha, Rāma's father.

claims.statement: In the youth narrative Sampati shields him from Surya's heat and has his own wings burned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah masa mudanya, Sampati melindunginya dari panas Surya dan terbakar sayapnya.

claims.statement: Jatayu tries to save Sita from Ravana's abduction but is defeated.
claims.statement_id: Jatayu berusaha menyelamatkan Sita dari penculikan Ravana tetapi dikalahkan.
claims.quote: According to the epic, the rakshasa Ravana was abducting the avatar of Lakshmi, Sita, when Jatayu tried to rescue her. Jatayu fought valiantly with Ravana, but as Jatayu was very old, Ravana soon defeated him,

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts dying Jatayu telling Rama what happened to Sita.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan Jatayu yang sekarat memberi tahu Rama apa yang terjadi pada Sita.
claims.quote:
On the morrow the brethren went forth again in
quest of the lost one. They came to the place where
Jatayus lay dying, and that lordly bird spake to Rama
and related all that had befallen Sita and himself.

claims.statement: Searching for Sita, Rama and Lakshmana found the dying Jatayu, who told them of the battle with Ravana and that Ravana had headed south; Jatayu then died of his wounds and Rama performed his funeral rites.
claims.statement_id: Rama dan Lakshmana, saat mencari Sita, menemukan Jatayu yang sekarat; ia menceritakan pertarungannya dengan Ravana dan memberi tahu bahwa Ravana menuju selatan, lalu mati karena lukanya, dan Rama melakukan upacara pemakamannya.
claims.quote: Rama and Lakshmana, while searching for Sita, chanced upon the stricken and dying Jatayu, who informed them of the battle with Ravana, and told them that Ravana had headed south. Jatayu then died of his wounds and Rama performed his final funeral rites.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling the Monarch of Vultures, asleep on a mountain top, hears Sita, wakes and darts upon Ravana like Indra's thunderbolt; a fierce battle is fought in mid air.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penceritaan Mackenzie, Raja Burung Nasar yang tertidur di puncak gunung mendengar jeritan Sita, terbangun, dan menyambar Ravana seperti petir Indra; pertempuran sengit terjadi di udara.
claims.quote: Monarch of Vultures, who lay asleep on a mountain top, heard her and awoke; he darted upon Ravana like to the thunderbolt of Indra. A fierce battle was fought in mid air.

Bhima found that he had sunk down to the city of

the young warrior, whom he desired greatly to
behold.

claims.quote: Chamunda (Sanskrit: चामुण्डा, IAST: Cāmuṇḍā), also known as Chamundeshwari, Chamundi or is a fearsome form of Chandi, the Hindu mother goddess, Mahadevi and is one of the seven Matrikas.

claims.statement: She is also one of the Yoginis attending Parvati.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga salah satu Yogini yang mengiringi Parvati.
claims.quote: She is also one of the chief Yoginis, a group of sixty-four or eighty-one Tantric goddesses, who are attendants of the warrior goddess Parvati. The name is a combination of Chanda and Munda, two demons whom Chamunda killed. She is closely associated with Mahakali or Durga.

claims.statement: Her name combines Chanda and Munda, two demons she kills.
claims.statement_id: Namanya menggabungkan nama Chanda dan Munda, dua demon yang dibunuhnya.
claims.quote: She is also one of the chief Yoginis, a group of sixty-four or eighty-one Tantric goddesses, who are attendants of the warrior goddess Parvati. The name is a combination of Chanda and Munda, two demons whom Chamunda killed. She is closely associated with Mahakali or Durga.

claims.statement: She is often depicted living in cremation grounds or near sacred fig trees.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan tinggal di tempat pembakaran jenazah atau dekat pohon ara suci.
claims.quote: The goddess is often portrayed as residing in cremation grounds or near holy fig trees. The goddess is worshipped by ritual animal sacrifices along with offerings of wine. The practice of animal sacrifices has become less common with Vaishnavite influences.

claims.statement: Later depictions show her as a skeletal old woman with sunken eyes.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran belakangan memperlihatkannya sebagai perempuan tua menyerupai kerangka dengan mata cekung.
claims.quote: In  early representations of Chamunda, she is given a ferocious visage, but with a feminine figure and elegant features. However, in later representations she is generally depicted as a skeletal old women wearing an elephant or tiger hide. She is shown to have sunken eyes, dishevelled hair.

claims.statement: She is depicted standing or sitting on a corpse or a vanquished demon.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berdiri atau duduk di atas jasad atau demon yang dikalahkan.
claims.quote: She is standing or sitting upon a 'shava' or corpse or sitting on a 'preta' or vanquished demon.

claims.statement: In Pargiter's translation of the Devi-Mahatmya, when Ambika is wrathful at her foes, Kali of the terrible countenance suddenly issues from her forehead.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Devi-Mahatmya terjemahan Pargiter, ketika Ambika murka kepada para musuh, Kali yang berwajah mengerikan tiba-tiba keluar dari dahinya.
claims.quote: Thereat Ambikā uttered her wrath aloud against those foes, and her countenance then grew dark as ink in her wrath. Out from the surface of her forehead, which was rugged with frowns, issued suddenly Kālī of the terrible countenance

claims.statement: Kali is described as decorated with a garland of skulls, clad in a tiger's skin, appalling in her emaciated flesh, exceedingly wide of mouth with her tongue lolling out, and having deep-sunk reddish eyes.
claims.statement_id: Kali digambarkan berhias kalung tengkorak, berbalut kulit harimau, bertubuh kurus mengerikan, bermulut sangat lebar dengan lidah terjulur, dan bermata merah cekung.
claims.quote: decorated with a garland of skulls, clad in a tiger’s skin, very appalling because of her emaciated flesh, exceedingly wide of mouth, lolling out her tongue terribly, having deep-sunk reddish eyes

claims.statement: Kali fell impetuously upon the great Asuras, dealing slaughter among the host, and devoured that army of the gods' foes.
claims.statement_id: Kali menyerbu para Asura besar dengan ganas, membantai pasukan itu, dan melahap pasukan musuh para dewa di sana.
claims.quote: She fell upon the great Asuras impetuously, dealing slaughter among the host, and devoured that army of the gods’ foes there.

claims.statement: The goddess, mounting her great lion, rushed at Caṇḍa, seized him by the hair and struck off his head with her sword.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewi menunggangi singa besarnya, menyerbu Caṇḍa, menjambak rambutnya, dan memenggal kepalanya dengan pedang.
claims.quote: And the goddess, mounting upon her great lion, rushed at Caṇḍa, and seizing him by his hair struck off his head with her sword.

claims.statement: Muṇḍa also rushed at her when he saw Caṇḍa laid low, and she felled him to the ground, stricken with her scimitar in her fury.
claims.statement_id: Muṇḍa juga menyerbunya ketika melihat Caṇḍa tumbang, dan ia pun dirobohkan oleh pedang lengkungnya dalam amarah.
claims.quote: And Muṇḍa also rushed at her when he saw Caṇḍa laid low; him also she felled to the ground, stricken with her scymitar in her fury.

claims.statement: Caṇḍikā declares that because Kali seized and brought Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa she shall be famed in the world by the name Cāmuṇḍā.
claims.statement_id: Caṇḍikā menyatakan bahwa karena Kali menangkap dan membawa Caṇḍa dan Muṇḍa, ia akan termasyhur di dunia dengan nama Cāmuṇḍā.
claims.quote: Because thou hast seized both Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa and brought them, thou, O goddess, shalt therefore be famed in the world by the name Cāmuṇḍā!

claims.statement: According to the Devi Mahatmya, Chamunda emerged from between the eyebrows of the goddess Kaushiki, created from the 'sheath' of Durga, and was assigned to eliminate the demons Chanda and Munda, servants of the demon kings Shumbha-Nisumbha.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Devi Mahatmya, Chamunda muncul dari tengah alis dewi Kaushiki, yang tercipta dari "sarung" Durga, dan diberi tugas membinasakan demon Chanda dan Munda, pelayan raja demon Shumbha-Nisumbha.
claims.quote: Chamunda emerged from middle of eyebrows of goddess Kaushiki, a goddess created from the "sheath" of Durga and was assigned the task of eliminating the demons Chanda and Munda, servants of demon kings Shumbha-Nisumbha.

claims.statement: According to another legend, Chamunda appeared from the frown of the benign goddess Parvati to kill the demons Chanda and Munda.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda lain, Chamunda muncul dari kerutan dahi dewi Parvati yang lembut untuk membunuh demon Chanda dan Munda.
claims.quote: According to another legend, Chamunda appeared from the frown of the benign goddess Parvati to kill demons Chanda and Munda.

claims.statement: In the text Kali is given the epithet Chamunda, so the Devi Mahatmya identifies Chamunda with Kali.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks itu Kali diberi gelar Chamunda, sehingga Devi Mahatmya menyamakan Chamunda dengan Kali.
claims.quote: Kali is given the epithet Chamunda in the text. Thus, the Devi Mahatmya identifies Chamunda with Kali.

claims.statement: The Varaha Purana text mentions Chamunda and Kali as two separate goddesses, unlike the Devi Mahatmya.
claims.statement_id: Teks Varaha Purana menyebut Chamunda dan Kali sebagai dua dewi yang terpisah, berbeda dari Devi Mahatmya.
claims.quote: The Varaha Purana text mentions two separate goddesses Chamunda and Kali, unlike Devi Mahatmya.

claims.statement: According to the Matsya Purana, Chamunda with the other matrikas was created by Shiva to help him kill the demon Andhakasura.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Matsya Purana, Chamunda bersama para matrika lain diciptakan Shiva untuk membantunya membunuh demon Andhakasura.
claims.quote: She with other matrikas was created by Shiva to help him kill the demon Andhakasura

claims.statement: The quality of drinking blood is a characteristic of all the Matrikas, and of Chamunda in particular.
claims.statement_id: Sifat meminum darah merupakan ciri semua Matrika, terutama Chamunda.
claims.quote: This quality of drinking blood is a characteristic of all Matrikas, and Chamunda in particular.

claims.statement_id: Para Matrika adalah dewi ibu yang menakutkan, penculik dan pemakan anak, yaitu lambang wabah, demam, kelaparan, dan penyakit pada masa kanak-kanak.
claims.quote: The Matrikas are fearsome mother goddesses, abductors and eaters of children; that is, they were emblematic of childhood pestilence, fever, starvation, and disease.

claims.statement: Chamunda is the only Matrika who is a Shakti of the great Goddess Devi rather than a male god, and the only one who enjoys independent worship of her own.
claims.statement_id: Chamunda satu-satunya Matrika yang merupakan Shakti Dewi agung, bukan dewa lelaki, dan juga satu-satunya yang menikmati pemujaan mandiri.
claims.quote: Chamunda is the only Matrika who is a Shakti of the great Goddess Devi rather than a male god. She is also the only Matrika who enjoys independent worship of her own

claims.quote: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar claims that Chamunda was originally a tribal goddess, worshipped by the tribals of the Vindhya mountains range in central India.

claims.quote: These characteristics, a contrast to the typical depictions of Hindu goddesses with beautiful faces, symbolise the inevitability of old age, death, decay and destruction.

claims.statement: Besides the usual meaning as slayer of the demons Chanda and Munda, the Devi Purana explains that Chanda means terrible while Munda stands for Brahma's head or lord or husband.
claims.statement_id: Selain makna lazim sebagai pembunuh demon Chanda dan Munda, Devi Purana memberi penjelasan lain: Chanda berarti mengerikan, sedangkan Munda berarti kepala, tuan, atau suami Brahma.
claims.quote: Apart from the usual meaning of Chamunda as the slayer of demons Chanda and Munda, the Devi Purana gives a different explanation: Chanda means terrible while Munda stands for Brahma's head or lord or husband.

claims.statement: Kinnara is a Hindu and Buddhist mythological creature depicted as part human and part bird.
claims.statement_id: Kinnara adalah makhluk mitologi Hindu dan Buddha yang digambarkan sebagian manusia dan sebagian burung.
claims.quote: A kinnara (Sanskrit: किन्नर Kiṃnara) is a creature from Hindu and Buddhist mythology.  They are described as part human and part bird, and have a strong association with music and love.

claims.statement: The creature is closely associated with music and love.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini erat dikaitkan dengan musik dan cinta.
claims.quote: A kinnara (Sanskrit: किन्नर Kiṃnara) is a creature from Hindu and Buddhist mythology.  They are described as part human and part bird, and have a strong association with music and love. Believed to come from the Himalayas, they often watch over the well-being of humans in times of trouble or danger. An ancient Indian string instrument is known as the Kinnari veena.

claims.statement: Kinnaras are believed to come from the Himalayas and watch over human well being in danger.
claims.statement_id: Kinnara diyakini berasal dari Himalaya dan menjaga kesejahteraan manusia saat bahaya.
claims.quote: Believed to come from the Himalayas, they often watch over the well-being of humans in times of trouble or danger.

claims.statement: In Southeast Asian traditions female kinnaris have female body parts and swan wings and tail.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Asia Tenggara, kinnari perempuan memiliki bagian tubuh perempuan dan sayap serta ekor angsa.
claims.quote: kinnaris have the head, torso, and arms of a woman and the wings, tail and feet of a swan.

claims.statement: Schafer distinguishes kinnara from kalavinka despite their frequent confusion in East Asian art.
claims.statement_id: Schafer membedakan kinnara dari kalavinka meski keduanya sering tertukar dalam seni Asia Timur.
claims.quote: Edward H. Schafer notes that in East Asian religious art, the kinnara is often confused with the Kalaviṅka, which is also a half-human, half-bird hybrid creature, but that the two are actually distinct and unrelated.

claims.statement: South Indian villagers regard her as a guardian deity.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk desa India Selatan memandangnya sebagai dewi penjaga.
claims.quote: She is considered as a guardian deity (kaval deivam) by many South Indian village dwellers.

claims.statement: The Tamil name Mari means rain and Amman means mother.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tamil Mari berarti hujan dan Amman berarti ibu.
claims.quote: The word Mari (pronunciation: /mɒri/) has the Sangam Tamil origin meaning "Rain", and the Dravidian root term Amman means "Mother". She was worshipped by the ancient Tamil as the bringer of rain and also the bringer of prosperity, since the abundance of their crops was dependent largely upon adequate rainfall.

claims.quote: The chief deity of the temple, Sri Mariamman, is associated with the sustaining and life-giving properties of rain

claims.statement: Tripura Sundari is a Shakta goddess belonging to the ten Mahavidyas.
claims.statement_id: Tripura Sundari adalah dewi Shakta yang termasuk sepuluh Mahavidya.
claims.quote: is a Hindu goddess revered primarily within the Shaktism tradition and recognized as one of the ten Mahavidyas.

claims.statement: Her other names include Lalita, Shodashi, Kamakshi, and Rajarajeshvari.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya Lalita, Shodashi, Kamakshi, dan Rajarajeshvari.

claims.quote: She signifies the most beautiful woman across the three realms,

claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Srikula ia dipandang sebagai dewi utama Sri Vidya dan Mahavidya tertinggi.
claims.quote: According to the Srikula tradition in Shaktism, Tripura Sundari is the foremost of the Mahavidyas, the supreme divinity of Hinduism and also the primary goddess of Sri Vidya. The Tripura Upanishad places her as the ultimate Shakti (energy, power) of the universe. She is described as the supreme consciousness, ruling from above Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.

claims.statement: The Lalita Sahasranama recounts her battle with Bhandasura.
claims.statement_id: Lalita Sahasranama menuturkan pertempurannya dengan Bhandasura.
claims.quote: The Lalita Sahasranama narrates the cosmic battle between Lalita Tripura Sundari and the demon Bhandasura,

claims.statement_id: Laman pariwisata India menuturkan legenda bahwa Tripura Sundari muncul dalam mimpi raja Dhanya Manikya dan memerintahkan pemujaannya dekat Udaipur.
claims.quote: King Dhanya Manikya of Tripura dreamt of Goddess Tripura Sundari, who instructed him to start her worship at a hill near Udaipur.

claims.statement: Preta is a supernatural being suffering extreme hunger and thirst in Asian religious traditions.
claims.statement_id: Preta merupakan makhluk gaib yang dalam tradisi agama Asia mengalami penderitaan serta lapar dan haus ekstrem.
claims.quote: is the Sanskrit name for a type of supernatural being described in Hinduism, Buddhism, Taoism, and Chinese folk religion as undergoing suffering greater than that of humans, particularly an extreme level of hunger and thirst.

claims.statement: The term hungry ghost mainly fits East Asian adaptations; the early Petavatthu has more varied forms.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan hantu lapar terutama sesuai adaptasi Asia Timur; Petavatthu awal memuat bentuk yang lebih beragam.
claims.quote: Preta is often translated into English as "hungry ghost" from the Chinese and East Asian adaptations. In early sources such as the Petavatthu, they are much more varied. The descriptions below apply mainly in this narrower context.

claims.statement: In the discussed belief past life karma causes insatiable hunger.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keyakinan yang dibahas, karma kehidupan lalu mengakibatkan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan.
claims.quote: As a result of their karma, they are afflicted with an insatiable hunger for a particular substance or object.

claims.statement: Preta traditions originate in Indian religions and spread to East Asia through Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi preta berasal dari agama India dan menyebar ke Asia Timur melalui Buddhisme.
claims.quote: Preta have their origins in Indian religions and have been adopted into East Asian religions via the spread of Buddhism. Through the belief and influence of Hinduism and Buddhism in much of Asia, preta figure appear prominently in the cultures of India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Mongolia, Tibet, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar.

claims.statement: Preta in Sanskrit means a departed or deceased person.
claims.statement_id: Preta dalam bahasa Sanskerta berarti orang yang telah pergi atau meninggal.
claims.quote: The Sanskrit term प्रेत preta means "departed, deceased, a dead person", from pra-ita, literally "gone forth, departed". In Classical Sanskrit, the term refers to the spirit of any dead person, but especially before the obsequial rites are performed, but also more narrowly to a ghost or evil being.

claims.statement: In the Tirokudda Kanda, hungry shades live on gifts from the living.

claims.quote:
They live on what is given here,

claims.statement: Vritra is a danava personifying drought and opposing Indra.
claims.statement_id: Vritra adalah danava yang mempersonifikasikan kekeringan dan menjadi lawan Indra.
claims.quote: He serves as the personification of drought, and is an adversary of the king of the devas, Indra.

claims.statement: He appears as a human like serpent blocking Rigvedic rivers.
claims.statement_id: Ia tampil sebagai ular menyerupai manusia yang menghalangi aliran sungai Rigveda.
claims.quote: He appears as a human-like serpent blocking the course of the Rigvedic rivers

claims.statement: Indra kills him with a newly forged vajra.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibunuh Indra dengan vajra yang baru dibuat.
claims.quote: and is slain by Indra with his newly forged vajra.

claims.statement: His name is explained as cover or obstacle, linked to holding back waters.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dijelaskan berarti penutup atau penghalang, berkaitan dengan penahanan air.
claims.quote: Vritra literally means "cover, obstacle", in reference of him holding back the waters. It stems from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥trás, from the Proto-Indo-European root *wer- "to cover, to obstruct". The Indo-Iranian word is also found in Avestan as vərəθraγna (Vedic vṛtraghná), literally "(one who) slays obstacles".

claims.statement: The battle narrative says Vritra breaks Indra's jaws before being defeated.
claims.statement_id: Kisah pertempuran menyebut Vritra mematahkan rahang Indra sebelum dikalahkan.
claims.quote: Vritra broke Indra's two jaws during the battle, but was then thrown down by Indra and, in falling, crushed the fortresses that had already been shattered. For this feat, Indra became known as "Vṛtrahan" (lit. "Slayer of Vritra" and also as "slayer of the first-born of dragons").

claims.statement: Mackenzie's retelling depicts Vritra holding cloud cattle captive in his mountain fortress.
claims.statement_id: Retelling Mackenzie menggambarkan Vritra menahan ternak awan dalam benteng gunungnya.
claims.quote:
According to Vedic myth, Indra achieved his first
great victory immediately after birth. Vritra, “the encompasser”,
the Demon of Drought, was holding captive
in his mountain fortress the cloud-cattle which he had
harried in the approved manner of the Aryan raiders.[43]
Mankind entreated the aid of the gods, “the shining
ones, the world guardians”:

claims.statement: A Rigveda hymn to Indra says Indra slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
claims.statement_id: Himne Rigveda untuk Indra menyebut Indra membunuh Sang Naga, lalu menyingkapkan air dan membelah saluran arus deras pegunungan.
claims.quote: I will declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.

claims.statement: The same hymn says Indra smote Vritra into pieces with his thunder, and the Dragon lies prostrate on the earth like felled tree trunks.
claims.statement_id: Himne yang sama menyebut Indra menghancurkan Vritra dengan petirnya; Sang Naga rebah di tanah seperti batang pohon yang ditebang.
claims.quote: Indra with his own great and deadly thunder smote into pieces Vṛitra, worst of Vṛitras. As trunks of trees, what time the axe hath felled them, low on the earth so lies the prostrate Dragon.

claims.statement: Vritra is described as footless and handless yet still challenging Indra, who struck him with a bolt between the shoulders, leaving him with scattered limbs.
claims.statement_id: Vritra digambarkan tanpa kaki dan tangan namun tetap menantang Indra, yang menghantamnya dengan petir di antara kedua bahu hingga anggota tubuhnya tercerai-berai.
claims.quote: Footless and handless still he challenged Indra, who smote him with his bolt between the shoulders. Emasculate yet claiming manly vigour, thus Vṛitra lay with scattered limbs dissevered.

claims.statement: A footnote to the hymn translation says Vritra is sometimes also named Ahi and interprets him as vapour shut up in a cloud, which Indra divides with his thunderbolt so that rain descends.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah catatan kaki pada terjemahan himne itu menyebut Vritra kadang juga dinamai Ahi dan menafsirkannya sebagai kumpulan uap yang terkurung awan, yang dibelah Indra dengan petirnya sehingga hujan turun.
claims.quote: Vṛitra, sometimes also named Ahi, is nothing more than the accumulation of vapour, condensed or figuratively shut up in, or obstructed by, a cloud. Indra, with his thunderbolt, or atmospheric or electrical influence, divides the aggregated mass, and vent is given to the rain which then descends upon the earth.

claims.statement: The translation notes that the Dragon of the hymn is Ahi, literally a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Catatan terjemahan menjelaskan bahwa Sang Naga dalam himne itu adalah Ahi, yang secara harfiah berarti ular.
claims.quote: The Dragon: Ahi, literally a serpent.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling, the dragon Vritra roared when Indra drew nigh, whereat heaven shook and the gods retreated.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penceritaan ulang Mackenzie, naga Vritra mengaum ketika Indra mendekat, sehingga langit bergetar dan para dewa mundur.
claims.quote: The dragon Vritra roared when Indra drew nigh; whereat heaven shook and the gods retreated.

claims.statement: Mackenzie relates the Mahabharata version: in the Krita Age a host of danavas, so strongly armed that they were invincible, selected the dragon Vritra as their leader and waged war on the gods, scattering them.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan versi Mahabharata: pada Zaman Krita sekelompok danava yang bersenjata kuat memilih naga Vritra sebagai pemimpin dan memerangi para dewa, yang mereka cerai-beraikan.
claims.quote: It is related that in the Krita Age (the first Age of the Universe) a host of Dānāvas (giants and demons) were so strongly armed that they were invincible in battle. They selected the dragon Vritra as their leader, and waged war against the gods, whom they scattered in all directions.

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata narration given to King Yudhishthira, Vritra was an asura created by the artisan god Tvashtri to avenge Indra's killing of his son, known as Triśiras or Viśvarūpa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Mahabharata yang dituturkan kepada Raja Yudhishthira, Vritra adalah asura yang diciptakan dewa pengrajin Tvashtri untuk membalas terbunuhnya putranya, Trishiras atau Vishvarupa, oleh Indra.
claims.quote: As told in the narration given to King Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata, Vritra was an asura created by the artisan god Tvashtri to avenge the killing of his son known as Triśiras or Viśvarūpa by Indra.

claims.statement: In the Vedic account Vritra's mother Danu, who was also the mother of the danava race of asuras, was attacked and defeated by Indra with his thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Rigveda, ibu Vritra bernama Danu, yang juga ibu ras asura danava, diserang dan dikalahkan Indra dengan petirnya.
claims.quote: Vritra's mother, Danu, who was also the mother of the danava race of asuras, was then attacked and defeated by Indra with his thunderbolt.

claims.statement: Bhagavata Purana 6.9.18 says this very fearful demon, the son of Tvashta, covered all the planetary systems by austerity and was therefore named Vritra, one who covers everything.
claims.statement_id: Bhagavata Purana 6.9.18 menyebut iblis yang sangat menakutkan itu putra Tvashta yang menutupi semua dunia dengan tapa, sehingga dinamai Vritra, yaitu yang menutupi segalanya.
claims.quote: That very fearful demon, who was actually the son of Tvaṣṭā, covered all the planetary systems by dint of austerity. Therefore he was named Vṛtra, or one who covers everything.

claims.statement: A Puranic encyclopaedia entry records Vritra, written वृत्र in Devanagari, as a mighty and fierce asura.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia Purana mencatat Vritra, juga ditulis dalam aksara Dewanagari sebagai वृत्र, sebagai asura yang perkasa dan garang.
claims.quote: Vṛtra (वृत्र).—(VṚTRĀSURA). A mighty and fierce asura.

claims.statement: Yamuna is the goddess personifying the Yamuna river in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Yamuna adalah dewi personifikasi sungai Yamuna dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: The river is also worshipped as a Hindu goddess called Yamuna.

claims.statement: Early texts call her Yami and later literature Kalindi.
claims.statement_id: Teks awal menyebutnya Yami dan sastra kemudian Kalindi.
claims.quote: Yamuna is known as Yami in early texts, while in later literature she is called Kalindi.

claims.statement: She is called Surya and Sanjna's daughter and Yama's twin sister.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut putri Surya dan Sanjna serta saudari kembar Yama.
claims.quote: In Hindu scriptures, she is the daughter of Surya, the sun god, and Sanjna, the cloud goddess. She is also the twin sister of Yama, god of death.

claims.statement: She is one of Krishna's eight principal consorts.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan salah satu delapan pasangan utama Krishna.
claims.quote: She is associated with the deity Krishna as one of his eight principal consorts, called the Ashtabharya.

claims.statement: The Agni Purana depicts her as dark, mounted on a tortoise, and holding a water pot.
claims.statement_id: Agni Purana menggambarkannya berkulit gelap, bertunggangan kura-kura, dan membawa wadah air.
claims.quote: Yamuna's iconographic depiction is seen on temple doorjambs, paired with that of Ganga (the goddess of the Ganges), since the Gupta era.  The Agni Purana describes Yamuna as black in complexion, standing on her mount, the tortoise, and holding a water pot in her hand. In an ancient painting she is shown as a beautiful maiden standing on the banks of the river.

claims.statement: Mackenzie quotes a hymn recounting Yami asking her brother Yama to marry.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mengutip himne yang menuturkan Yami mengajak saudaranya Yama menikah.
claims.quote:
In one of the hymns[103] Yami is the wooer of her
brother Yama. She declares that they were at the beginning
intended by the gods to be husband and wife,
but Yama replies:

claims.statement: Kamadhenu or Surabhi is a bovine goddess and mother of all cows in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Kamadhenu atau Surabhi adalah dewi sapi dan ibu semua sapi dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is a divine bovine-goddess described in Hinduism as the mother of all cows.

claims.statement: She is a miraculous cow providing whatever her owner desires.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan sapi ajaib yang menyediakan apa pun yang diinginkan pemiliknya.
claims.quote: She is a miraculous cow of plenty who provides her owner whatever they desire

claims.statement: One iconographic form is a white cow with a woman's head, bird wings, and peafowl tail.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu ikonografinya berupa sapi putih berkepala perempuan, bersayap burung, dan berekor merak.
claims.quote: she is generally depicted as a white cow with a female head and breasts, the wings of a bird, and the tail of a peafowl

claims.statement: Her origin accounts differ: emerging from ocean churning or being Daksha's daughter and Kashyapa's wife.
claims.statement_id: Kisah asalnya berbeda: muncul dari pengadukan samudra atau menjadi putri Daksha dan istri Kashyapa.
claims.quote: Hindu scriptures provide diverse accounts of the birth of Kamadhenu. While some narrate that she emerged from the churning of the cosmic ocean, others describe her as the daughter of the creator god Daksha, and as the wife of the sage Kashyapa.

claims.statement: She produces milk for her sage master's offerings and can produce warriors to protect him.
claims.statement_id: Ia menghasilkan susu untuk persembahan sang resi dan dapat menghasilkan prajurit untuk melindunginya.
claims.quote: Kamadhenu plays the important role of providing milk and milk products to be used in her sage-master's oblations; she is also capable of producing fierce warriors to protect him.

claims.statement: Kamadhenu means a cow providing all that is desired; Nandini sometimes bears the epithet or is called her daughter.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan Kamadhenu berarti sapi yang menyediakan semua yang diinginkan; Nandini kadang mendapat sebutan itu atau disebut putrinya.
claims.quote: In the Mahabharata and Devi Bhagavata Purana, in the context of the birth of Bhishma, the cow Nandini is given the epithet Kamadhenu. In other instances, Nandini is described as the cow-daughter of Surabhi-Kamadhenu.

claims.statement: In Ganguli's Mahabharata translation Surabhi and Kasyapa parent Nandini, the wish granting cow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata terjemahan Ganguli, Surabhi dan Kashyapa menjadi orang tua sapi Nandini yang memenuhi keinginan.
claims.quote:
Surabhi, who, O bull of
      Bharata’s race, for benefiting the world, brought forth, by her connection
      with Kasyapa, a daughter (Nandini) in the form of a cow. ... Nandini, was the cow of plenty (capable of granting every
      desire).

claims.statement: Kumbhakarna is a mighty rakshasa and Ravana's younger brother in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Kumbhakarna adalah rakshasa perkasa dan adik Ravana dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote: Kumbhakarna (Sanskrit: कुम्भकर्ण, lit. pot-eared) is a powerful rakshasa and younger brother of Ravana from the Hindu epic Ramayana. Despite his gigantic size and appetite, he is described as a virtuous character and a great warrior in Hindu texts. He is said to have slaughtered 8,000 vanaras over the course of Rama's mission to rescue Sita.

claims.statement: Hindu texts depict him as gigantic and voracious but also a virtuous warrior.
claims.statement_id: Teks Hindu menggambarkannya bertubuh raksasa dan berselera makan besar tetapi juga kesatria berbudi.
claims.quote: Despite his gigantic size and appetite, he is described as a virtuous character and a great warrior in Hindu texts.

claims.statement: In the version summarized by the article Brahma modifies his curse to six months asleep and six months awake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi yang diringkas artikel, Brahma mengubah kutukannya menjadi tidur enam bulan dan bangun enam bulan.
claims.quote: he commuted the curse to have the rakshasa sleep for six months at a time, and wake up for other six months to wreak havoc and devour to his heart's content.

claims.statement: In another retelling Saraswati makes his tongue request a sleeping bed instead of Indra's throne.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling lain, Saraswati membuat lidahnya meminta tempat tidur alih-alih takhta Indra.
claims.quote: When Kumbhakarna asked for his boon, his tongue was tied by the goddess Saraswati, who acted on Indra's request. Instead of asking for Indrāsana (the throne of Indra), he asked for Nidrāsana (a bed for sleeping). It is also said that he intended to ask for Nirdevatvam (annihilation of the devas) and instead asked for Nidravatvam (sleep). His request was instantly granted.

claims.statement: In this retelling he sleeps again after his appetite is satisfied.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling ini ia tidur lagi setelah rasa laparnya terpenuhi.
claims.quote: Brahma reduced it to sleeping for six months, after which he would sleep again as soon as his appetite was satisfied.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling he sleeps six months and wakes for only one day.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling Mackenzie, ia tidur enam bulan dan bangun hanya satu hari.
claims.quote:
Brahma intervened and decreed that he
would sleep for six months and then awaken for one day
only.

claims.statement: Vahana denotes beings, usually animals or mythical creatures, serving as Hindu deities' vehicles.
claims.statement_id: Vahana adalah golongan makhluk, biasanya hewan atau makhluk mitos, yang menjadi kendaraan dewa Hindu.
claims.quote: denotes the being, typically an animal or mythical entity, a particular Hindu deity is said to use as a vehicle.

claims.statement: Deities are depicted riding them or vahanas stand beside deities as attributes.
claims.statement_id: Dewa digambarkan menaikinya atau vahana berada di samping dewa sebagai atribut.
claims.quote: Deities are often depicted riding (or simply mounted upon) the vāhana. Other times, the vāhana is depicted at the deity's side or symbolically represented as a divine attribute.

claims.statement: The Sanskrit root vah means to carry or transport.
claims.statement_id: Akar Sanskerta vah berarti membawa atau mengangkut.
claims.quote: Vah in Sanskrit means to carry or transport. The word also means 'vehicle' in Sanskrit and other Indian languages.

claims.statement: Nandi as Shiva's vehicle symbolizes strength; Saraswati's hamsa symbolizes wisdom.
claims.statement_id: Nandi sebagai kendaraan Shiva melambangkan kekuatan; hamsa Saraswati melambangkan kebijaksanaan.
claims.quote: Nandi the bull and vehicle of Shiva, represents strength and virility. ... The hamsa, the vehicle of Saraswati, represents wisdom, grace, and beauty.

claims.statement: Divine vehicles can also symbolize negative forces overcome by their deities.
claims.statement_id: Kendaraan ilahi juga dapat melambangkan kekuatan negatif yang ditaklukkan dewanya.
claims.quote: However, a divine mount also symbolizes the negative or destructive forces over which the deity triumphs. Mounted on Parvani, Kartikeya reins in the peacock's vanity. Seated upon Dinka, the rat (Mushika), Ganesha subdues erratic thoughts, which multiply like rodents in the dark. Shani, the protector of property, rides a vulture, raven, or crow, whose thieving tendencies he represents.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling the white elephant Airavata is Indra's mount.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling Mackenzie, gajah putih Airavata menjadi tunggangan Indra.
claims.quote:
Indra was attended by a dog, as befitted a deity of[Pg 18]
primitive huntsmen. After the early Aryan period, he
showed less favour for his bays and chariot, and seated
himself upon a great white elephant, “the handsome and
ever victorious”, named Airavata; it “was furnished with
four tusks” and “resembled the mountain of Kailasa with
its summits”.

claims.statement: The vahana symbolically doubles as the deity's power, and also represents the devotee's mind, which the deity controls and guides.
claims.statement_id: Wahana secara simbolis menjadi kembaran kuasa sang dewa, dan juga melambangkan pikiran pemuja yang dikendalikan dan dibimbing sang dewa.
claims.quote: The vahana symbolically doubles as a deity's power. The vahana also represents the devotee's mind, which the deity controls and guides.

claims.statement: A vahana may act independently, yet it is functionally emblematic of, or viewed as an extension of, its "rider".
claims.statement_id: Wahana dapat bertindak mandiri, tetapi secara fungsional dianggap lambang atau perpanjangan dari "penunggangnya".
claims.quote: though the vāhana may act independently, they are still functionally emblematic of or even viewed as an extension of their

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata episode quoted in the article, Garuda goes for the pot of amrita; the Devas, Indra, even the Sun and Moon line up against him, but he defeats them all.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Mahabharata yang dikutip artikel ini, Garuda merebut kendi amrita: para Dewa, Indra, bahkan Matahari dan Bulan melawannya, tetapi ia mengalahkan mereka semua.
claims.quote: Garuḍa approached the pot of nectar, and Viśvakarmā who attacked him first was felled to the ground. The dust storm raised by the waving of Garuḍa’s wings blinded everybody. The Devas and Indra, nay, even the sun and the Moon lined up against Garuḍa, but he defeated them all

claims.statement: At his request, Vishnu granted that Garuda become his vehicle and be rendered immortal without tasting amrita.
claims.statement_id: Atas permintaannya, Wisnu mengabulkan agar Garuda menjadi wahananya dan abadi tanpa mencicipi amrita.
claims.quote: Garuḍa requested Viṣṇu that he should be made his (Viṣṇu's) vehicle and rendered immortal without his tasting amṛta. Both the boons were granted.

claims.statement: A giant mouse terrorized the child Ganesha's friends; Ganesha trapped it with his lasso and made it his mount.
claims.statement_id: Seekor tikus raksasa meneror teman-teman Ganesha yang masih kecil; Ganesha menjeratnya dengan laso dan menjadikannya tunggangan.
claims.quote: While Ganesha was still a child, a giant mouse began to terrorize his friends. Ganesha trapped the creature with his lasso (pasha) and made him his mount.

claims.statement: The peacock Paravani, Kartikeya's mount, was originally the demon Surapadma, and the rooster on his banner was originally the demon Krichi.
claims.statement_id: Merak wahana Kartikeya, Paravani, dahulu adalah iblis Surapadma, dan ayam jantan pada panjinya dahulu adalah iblis Krichi.
claims.quote: This peacock was originally a demon named Surapadma, while his banner's rooster was originally a demon named Krichi.

claims.statement: A statue of Nandi guards the entrance of virtually every Shiva temple, perpetually facing the inner shrine.
claims.statement_id: Patung Nandi menjaga pintu masuk hampir setiap kuil Siwa, menghadap ke bilik suci.
claims.quote: Since then a statue of Nandi has guarded the entrance of virtually every Shiva temple, perpetually facing the inner shrine.

claims.statement: Goddess Durga defeated the demon Mahishasura without the help of her vahana, a lion given to her by her father Himalaya.
claims.statement_id: Dewi Durga mengalahkan iblis Mahishasura tanpa bantuan wahananya, singa pemberian ayahnya Himalaya.
claims.quote: Goddess Durga defeated the demon Mahishasura without the help of her vahana, lion given to her by her father Himalaya.

claims.statement: Garuda, Vishnu's vehicle, is the enemy of all snakes, which are symbolic of death and the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Garuda, wahana Wisnu, dikenal sebagai musuh semua ular, yang melambangkan kematian dan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: The latter name is in reference to his role as the enemy of all snakes which are symbolic of death and the underworld.

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata Garuda eats evil men; once he swallowed a brahmana and his wife but had to spit them out because the priest burned his throat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata, Garuda memakan orang jahat; ia pernah menelan seorang brahmana dan istrinya, tetapi terpaksa memuntahkan mereka karena kerongkongannya terbakar.
claims.quote: In the Mahabharata Garuda eats evil men. In one episode he swallowed a brahmana and his wife but the priest burned Garuda's throat so much that he was compelled to spit the couple out.

claims.statement: In the Bhagavata Purana Garuda attacks the many-headed snake Kaliya, hitting him with his wings so hard that Kaliya hides in a pool of the Kalindi River.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavata Purana, Garuda menyerang ular berkepala banyak Kaliya dan memukulnya dengan sayap hingga Kaliya bersembunyi di kolam Sungai Kalindi.
claims.quote: In the Bhagavata Purana a legend is told where Garuda fights the fearsome many-headed snake Kaliya. ... Garuda attacked Kaliya, hitting him so hard with his wings that Kaliya hid in a pool of the Kalindi River.

claims.statement: Indra soon found out and, unconvinced by Garuda's motive that he needed the amrta as a ransom to free his mother from Kadru, fought the giant bird in an epic battle; Indra lost his thunderbolt but eventually retrieved the amrta.
claims.statement_id: Indra segera mengetahuinya dan, tidak yakin dengan alasan Garuda bahwa amrita itu diperlukan sebagai tebusan untuk membebaskan ibunya dari cengkeraman Kadru, melawan burung raksasa itu dalam pertempuran besar; Indra kehilangan petirnya, tetapi akhirnya berhasil merebut kembali amrita.
claims.quote: Indra soon found out and, unconvinced by Garuda's motive that he needed the amrta as a ransom to free his mother from the clutches of Kadru, fought the giant bird in an epic battle. Mighty Indra lost his famous thunderbolt in the clash but eventually managed to retrieve the amrta.

claims.statement: As king of the birds, Garuda threatened the Ocean that he would attack it incessantly if the sparrow's eggs were not given back; the Ocean relented and returned the eggs.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai raja burung, Garuda mengancam Samudra akan menyerangnya terus-menerus bila telur burung gereja itu tidak dikembalikan; Samudra mengalah dan mengembalikan telur-telur itu.
claims.quote: Garuda who, as king of the birds, felt sympathy and threatened the Ocean that if the eggs were not given back then Garuda himself would incessantly attack the Ocean. Ocean relented and returned the eggs to the ever grateful sparrow.

claims.statement: Indrajit or Meghanada is Ravana's eldest son and Lanka's crown prince in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Indrajit atau Meghanada adalah putra sulung Ravana dan putra mahkota Lanka dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote: was the eldest son of Ravana and the crown prince of Lanka,

claims.statement: He can fight from the sky while hidden behind clouds.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat bertempur dari langit sambil tersembunyi di balik awan.
claims.quote: Indrajita had the special ability to fight from the sky, hidden behind the clouds.

claims.statement: Indrajit means conqueror of Indra, linked to his victory over the deva king.
claims.statement_id: Nama Indrajit berarti penakluk Indra, berkaitan dengan kemenangannya atas raja para deva.
claims.quote: Indrajita had the special ability to fight from the sky, hidden behind the clouds. That is why both Rama and Lakshmana were defeated during the battle and were tied up by the snake. In Sanskrit, the literal translation of the name "Indrajita" (इन्द्रजित) is mentioned as the "Conqueror of Indra".

claims.statement: His mother is Mandodari, Ravana's wife.
claims.statement_id: Ibunya adalah Mandodari, istri Ravana.
claims.quote: Indrajita was the eldest son of Ravana and his wife Mandodari.

claims.statement: Sulochana is called his wife in later versions rather than the original epic.
claims.statement_id: Sulochana disebut sebagai istrinya dalam versi belakangan, bukan dalam epos asli.
claims.quote: His wife is not mentioned in the original epic; however in later versions of the epic, Sulochana

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Indrajit binding Hanuman with a magical serpent arrow.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mengisahkan Indrajit membelenggu Hanuman dengan anak panah sihir berwujud ular.
claims.quote:
the mighty Indrajit,
son of Ravana, hastened forth and shot a magic serpent-shaft
which enwrapped Hanuman like a noose, and rendered
him helpless.

claims.statement: Putana is a rakshasi killed by the infant Krishna in Hindu narratives.
claims.statement_id: Putana adalah rakshasi yang dibunuh Krishna saat masih bayi dalam kisah Hindu.
claims.quote: is a rakshasi (demoness) who was killed by the infant-god Krishna.

claims.statement: She disguises herself as a beautiful young woman.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai perempuan muda yang cantik.
claims.quote: Putana disguises herself as a young, beautiful woman

claims.statement: She tries to kill Krishna by nursing him with poisoned milk.
claims.statement_id: Ia mencoba membunuh Krishna dengan menyusui menggunakan susu beracun.
claims.quote: tries to kill the god by breast-feeding him poisoned milk;

claims.statement: Krishna sucks both milk and life from her breasts.
claims.statement_id: Krishna mengisap susu sekaligus nyawanya dari payudaranya.
claims.quote: Krishna sucks her milk as well as her life via her breasts.

claims.statement: Ancient Indian medical texts prescribe her worship to protect children from disease.
claims.statement_id: Teks medis India kuno menganjurkan pemujaannya untuk melindungi anak dari penyakit.
claims.quote: Ancient Indian medical texts prescribe her worship to protect children from diseases.

claims.statement: The Vedabase Bhagavata text says Putana attains a mother's position in the transcendental world after death.
claims.statement_id: Teks Bhagavata versi Vedabase menyatakan Putana memperoleh kedudukan ibu di dunia transendental setelah kematiannya.
claims.quote: she attained the position of a mother in the transcendental world

claims.statement: Vibhishana is Ravana's younger brother in the Ramayana and one of the Chiranjivis.

claims.statement: Although a rakshasa he leaves Ravana and joins Rama for dharma.
claims.statement_id: Meski rakshasa, ia meninggalkan Ravana dan bergabung dengan Rama demi dharma.
claims.quote: Vibhishana (Sanskrit: विभीषण, romanized: Vibhīṣaṇa, lit. 'formidable') is the younger brother of Ravana, the King of Lanka, in the ancient Indian epic Ramayana, and one of the eight Chiranjivis. claims.quote: Prince Vibhishana is portrayed as a pious and pure of heart in the epic. claims.statement: Ulupi is a naga princess in the Mahabharata, Kauravya's daughter and Arjuna's second wife.
claims.statement_id: Ulupi adalah putri naga dalam Mahabharata, putri Kauravya dan istri kedua Arjuna.
claims.quote: Ulupi (Ulūpī), also known as Uluchi and Ulupika, is a Naga princess mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. Ulupi is the daughter of the king Kauravya, and is the second wife of Arjuna. She also finds a mention in the Vishnu Purana and the Bhagavata Purana.

claims.statement: She meets and marries Arjuna during his exile and bears Iravan.
claims.statement_id: Ia bertemu dan menikah dengan Arjuna saat pengasingannya dan melahirkan Iravan.
claims.quote: Ulupi is said to have met and married Arjuna when he was in exile, and with whom she bore his son Iravan. She is also credited with redeeming Arjuna from the curse of the Vasus by restoring his life after he was slain in a battle by his son, Babhruvahana.

claims.statement: She revives Arjuna after Babhruvahana kills him, redeeming him from the Vasus' curse.
claims.statement_id: Ia menghidupkan kembali Arjuna setelah ia dibunuh Babhruvahana, sehingga membebaskannya dari kutukan Vasu.
claims.quote: Ulupi is said to have met and married Arjuna when he was in exile, and with whom she bore his son Iravan. She is also credited with redeeming Arjuna from the curse of the Vasus by restoring his life after he was slain in a battle by his son, Babhruvahana.

claims.statement: The Mahabharata names her in many ways, including Kauravyaduhita and Pannagi.
claims.statement_id: Mahabharata menyebutnya dengan banyak nama, termasuk Kauravyaduhita dan Pannagi.
claims.quote: Little is said about Ulupi in the Mahabharata. Ulupi is known by numerous names in the Mahabharata—Bhujagātmajā, Bhujagendrakanyakā, Bhujagottamā Kauravī, Kauravyaduhitā, Kauravyakulanandinī, Pannaganandinī, Pannagasutā, Pannagātmajā, Pannageśvarakanyā, Pannagī, and Uragātmajā.

claims.statement: She is depicted as a nagakanya, part woman and part serpent.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai nagakanya, sebagian perempuan dan sebagian ular.
claims.quote: Ulupi is described as a mythical form of a Nāgakanyā (Nāga princess), half-maiden and half-serpent.

claims.statement: Mackenzie calls Ulupi Iravat's mother and a serpent nymph, daughter of the naga king.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut Ulupi sebagai ibu Iravat dan nimfa ular, putri raja naga.
claims.quote:
brave Iravat, whose
mother was Ulupi, the serpent nymph, daughter of the
king of the Nagas.

claims.statement: Ulupi was the daughter of the Naga king Kauravya, who ruled the underwater kingdom of serpents in the Ganga; she was a well-trained warrior.
claims.statement_id: Ulupi adalah putri Raja Naga Kauravya, yang memerintah kerajaan ular di bawah air Sungai Gangga; ia seorang pejuang terlatih.
claims.quote: Ulupi was the daughter of the Naga King Kauravya. Her father ruled the underwater kingdom of serpents in the Ganga river. She was a well-trained warrior.

claims.statement: Ganga said Arjuna would be killed by his own son Babhruvahana and brought back to life when Ulupi placed the gem Nagamani on his chest; on her father's advice Ulupi incites Babhruvahana to fight Arjuna.
claims.statement_id: Gangga berkata Arjuna akan dibunuh putranya sendiri, Babhruvahana, dan dihidupkan kembali ketika Ulupi meletakkan permata Nagamani di dadanya; atas nasihat ayahnya, Ulupi menghasut Babhruvahana untuk melawan Arjuna.
claims.quote: Upon hearing him, Ganga said that Arjuna would be killed by his own son, Babhruvahana—Arjuna's son through Chitrangada—and brought back to life when Ulupi placed a gem called Nagamani on his chest. Following her father's advice, Ulupi instigates Babruvāhana to fight Arjuna.

claims.statement: Iravan is Arjuna and the naga princess Ulupi's son in the Mahabharata.
claims.statement_id: Iravan adalah putra Arjuna dan putri naga Ulupi dalam Mahabharata.
claims.quote: The son of Pandava prince Arjuna (one of the main heroes of the Mahabharata) and the Naga princess Ulupi,

claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi dewa utama dalam kultus Kuttantavar dan tokoh penting dalam tradisi Draupadi.
claims.quote: Iravan  also known as Iravat and Iravant, is a minor character from the Hindu epic Mahabharata. The son of Pandava prince Arjuna (one of the main heroes of the Mahabharata) and the Naga princess Ulupi, Iravan is the central deity of the cult of Kuttantavar (Kuttandavar) which is also the name commonly given to him in that tradition—and plays a major role in the sect of Draupadi.

claims.statement: The Mahabharata recounts his death on the eighth day of the Kurukshetra war.

claims.quote: The Mahabharata portrays Iravan as dying a heroic death on the 8th day of the 18-day Kurukshetra War, the epic's main subject. However, the South Indian traditions have a supplementary practice of honouring Aravan's self-sacrifice to the goddess Kali to ensure her favour and the victory of the Pandavas in the war.

claims.statement: South Indian traditions honor his sacrifice to Kali for the Pandavas' victory.

claims.statement: In Draupadi traditions Krishna allows Iravan's severed head to witness the whole war.

claims.quote: Krishna allows Aravan to witness the entire duration of the Mahabharata war through the eyes of his severed head.

claims.statement: Mackenzie calls brave Iravat one of the Pandava army's young heroes.

claims.quote:
Among the young heroes were Arjuna's two sons,
the noble and peerless Abhimanyu, whose mother was
Krishna's fair sister Subhadra, and brave Iravat,

claims.statement: Mucilinda is a naga protecting Shakyamuni Buddha from the elements after his awakening.
claims.statement_id: Mucilinda adalah naga yang melindungi Buddha Shakyamuni dari cuaca setelah pencerahannya.
claims.quote: Mucilinda (Sanskrit: मुचिलिन्द ; Pali: Mucalinda) is a nāga who protected Śākyamuni Buddha from the elements after his enlightenment.

claims.statement: His narrative recounts heavy rain and dark skies for seven days.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya menuturkan hujan deras dan langit gelap selama tujuh hari.
claims.quote: It is said that six weeks after Gautama Buddha began meditating under the Bodhi Tree, the heavens darkened for seven days, and a prodigious rain descended.

claims.statement: He emerges from beneath the earth and shields Buddha with his hood.
claims.statement_id: Ia muncul dari bawah tanah dan melindungi Buddha dengan tudungnya.
claims.quote: However, the mighty King of Serpents, Mucilinda, came from beneath the earth and protected with his hood the One who is the source of all protection.

claims.statement: The Mucalinda Sutta depicts the naga coiling around Buddha seven times.
claims.statement_id: Mucalinda Sutta menggambarkan naga melilit tubuh Buddha tujuh kali.
claims.quote: Mucalinda first appears in the Mucalinda Sutta, where it is described that the naga king protected Buddha from the elements by encircling Buddha's body seven times with his coils and standing with his hood spread over.

claims.statement: After the sky clears he becomes a youth and bows before Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Setelah langit cerah, ia menjadi pemuda dan bersujud di hadapan Buddha.
claims.quote: After Buddha finished meditating and the sky cleared, Mucalinda adopted the form of a youth and bowed before him.

claims.statement: The Udana 2.1 translation says the naga king Muccalinda coils around Buddha seven times and spreads his hood.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Udana 2.1 menyebut raja naga Muccalinda melilit Buddha tujuh kali dan membentangkan tudungnya.
claims.quote: encircling the Blessed One's body seven times with his coils — stood with his great hood spread over the Blessed One

claims.statement: Udana 2.1 says a great, out-of-season storm-cloud rose up, with seven days of rainy weather, cold winds and intense darkness.
claims.statement_id: Udana 2.1 menyebut awan badai besar di luar musim muncul, dengan tujuh hari cuaca hujan, angin dingin, dan kegelapan pekat.
claims.quote: And on that occasion a great, out-of-season storm-cloud rose up, with seven days of rainy weather, cold winds, & intense darkness.

claims.statement: In Udana 2.1 the naga king Muccalinda thinks that the Blessed One should not be disturbed by cold, by heat, or by the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun and creeping things.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Udana 2.1, raja naga Muccalinda berpikir agar Sang Bhagava tidak terganggu oleh dingin, panas, atau sentuhan lalat, nyamuk, angin, matahari, dan makhluk melata.
claims.quote: Don't let the Blessed One be disturbed by cold. Don't let the Blessed One be disturbed by heat. Don't let the Blessed One be disturbed by the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, & creeping things.

claims.statement: Once the sky had cleared, Muccalinda unraveled his coils from the Blessed One's body, dropped his own appearance and stood before him as a young man with hands before his heart, paying homage.
claims.statement_id: Setelah langit cerah, Muccalinda melepaskan lilitannya dari tubuh Sang Bhagava, meninggalkan wujudnya, dan berdiri di depannya sebagai pemuda dengan tangan di depan dada untuk memberi hormat.
claims.quote: Muccalinda the nāga king, realizing that the sky had cleared and was free of clouds, unraveled his coils from the body of the Blessed One, dropped his own appearance and, assuming the appearance of a young man, stood in front of the Blessed One with hands before his heart, paying homage.

claims.statement: The first existent artwork depicting Mucalinda comes from a 2nd-century BC stupa in Pauni, Maharashtra, where the naga has five heads and guards the Buddha's empty seat.
claims.statement_id: Karya seni tertua yang masih ada yang menggambarkan Mucalinda berasal dari stupa abad ke-2 SM di Pauni, Maharashtra, tempat naga itu digambarkan berkepala lima dan menjaga tempat duduk kosong Buddha.
claims.quote: The first existent artwork depicting Mucalinda comes from a 2nd-century BC stupa in Pauni, Maharashtra, where the naga is portrayed as having five heads and guarding Buddha's empty seat.

claims.statement: Contemporaneous artwork from Sanchi portrays him in zoo-anthropomorphic form, attended by a retinue of nagini.
claims.statement_id: Karya seni sezaman dari Sanchi menampilkannya berwujud setengah hewan dan manusia, dengan pengiring para nagini.
claims.quote: Contemporaneous artwork from Sanchi has him portrayed in zoo-anthropomorphic form and attended by a retinue of nagini.

claims.statement: According to the Lalitavistara Sutra, five weeks after his enlightenment the Buddha was in Mucilinda's domain; Mucilinda and nagas from the four cardinal directions coiled around his body seven times to shelter him from the bad weather for seven days and nights.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Lalitavistara Sutra, lima minggu setelah pencerahan, Buddha berada di wilayah Mucilinda; Mucilinda bersama naga dari empat penjuru melilit tubuhnya tujuh kali untuk melindunginya dari cuaca buruk selama tujuh hari tujuh malam.
claims.quote: According to the Lalitavistara Sutra, the Buddha found himself in the domain of Mucilinda five weeks after his enlightenment. Mucilinda, along with nāgas from the four cardinal directions, approached him and coiled around his body seven times to shelter him from the inclement weather. They did so for seven days and seven nights.

claims.statement: Art showing the Buddha with Mucalinda's hood over him might have been influenced by Jain art of Parshvanatha, himself shown as a man with a cobra-like hood.
claims.statement_id: Seni yang menggambarkan Buddha dengan tudung Mucalinda di atasnya mungkin dipengaruhi seni Jain tentang Parshvanatha, yang digambarkan sebagai manusia dengan tudung seperti kobra.
claims.quote: Art depicting the Buddha with Mucalinda's hood over him might have been influenced by Jain art of Parshvanatha, himself depicted as a man with a cobra-like hood.

claims.statement: The Dictionary of Pali Proper Names says the Buddha spent the third week after the Enlightenment at the tree; in a great shower of rain the Naga king Mucalinda of the tree sheltered him by winding his coils seven times around him and holding his hood over his head.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Nama-nama Pali menyebut Buddha menghabiskan minggu ketiga setelah pencerahan di pohon itu; saat hujan lebat, raja naga Mucalinda dari pohon itu melindunginya dengan melilitkan tubuhnya tujuh kali dan membentangkan tudung di atas kepala Buddha.
claims.quote: The Buddha spent there the third week after the Enlightenment. There was a great shower of rain, and the Naga king, Mucalinda, of the tree, sheltered the Buddha by winding his coils seven times round the Buddhas body and holding his hood over the Buddhas head

claims.statement: The Udana Commentary, according to the same dictionary, adds that the space provided by the Naga's coils was as large as the floor space of the Lohapasada and that the Naga king lived in a pond near the tree.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Udana, menurut kamus yang sama, menambahkan bahwa ruang yang dibentuk lilitan sang naga seluas lantai Lohapasada dan bahwa raja naga itu tinggal di kolam dekat pohon.
claims.quote: the space provided by the Nagas coils was as large as the floor space of the Lohapasada and that the Naga king lived in a pond near the tree.

claims.statement: A Sanskrit dictionary records Mucilinda as the name of a Naga who sheltered the Buddha from a violent storm by coiling himself round him.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Sansekerta mencatat Mucilinda sebagai nama seorang Naga yang melindungi Buddha dari badai dahsyat dengan melilitkan dirinya mengelilingi Buddha.
claims.quote: Name of a Nāga (who sheltered the Buddha from a violent storm by coiling himself round him)

claims.statement: Udana 2.1 sets the story at Uruvelā, on the bank of the Nerañjarā River at the root of the Muccalinda tree, when the Blessed One was newly awakened.
claims.statement_id: Udana 2.1 menempatkan kisah ini di Uruvela, di tepi Sungai Neranjara, di akar pohon Muccalinda, ketika Sang Bhagava baru saja tercerahkan.
claims.quote: I have heard that on one occasion, the Blessed One was staying at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River at the root of the Muccalinda tree, newly awakened.

claims.quote: is a seven-headed flying horse, created during the churning of the ocean.

claims.statement: LACMA describes ganas as rotund gnomes dancing and playing music for Shiva and Parvati.

claims.quote: They are envisioned as rotund gnomes, often rambunctious and full of zest. They dance and play music for Shiva and his wife Parvati.

claims.statement: The word gana in Sanskrit and Pali means flock, troop, multitude, number, tribe, category, series or clan, and can also refer to a body of attendants.
claims.statement_id: Kata gana dalam bahasa Sanskerta dan Pali berarti kawanan, pasukan, banyak, jumlah, suku, kategori, deret, atau klan, dan juga dapat dipakai untuk merujuk pada rombongan pengiring.
claims.quote: in Sanskrit and Pali means "flock, troop, multitude, number, tribe, category, series, or clan". It can also be used to refer to a "body of attendants"

claims.statement: LACMA describes ganas (troop or multitude) as types of demigods who serve as attendants for the Hindu god Shiva.
claims.statement_id: LACMA menyebut gana (kawanan atau banyak) sebagai jenis dewa setengah yang melayani dewa Hindu Shiva sebagai pengiring.
claims.quote: Ganas (troop or multitude) are types of demigods who serve as attendants for the Hindu god Shiva.

claims.statement: According to the LACMA curatorial notes, hosts of ganas are often depicted accompanying Shiva and Parvati in later group representations of their Holy Family.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan kurator LACMA, rombongan gana sering digambarkan menyertai Shiva dan Parvati dalam penggambaran kelompok keluarga suci mereka yang lebih belakangan.
claims.quote: Hosts of ganas are often depicted accompanying Shiva and Parvati in later group representations of their Holy Family.

claims.statement: The LACMA sculpture shows a gana who uses percussion mallets to play an hourglass-shaped drum tied to his ample girth while he dances to its beat.
claims.statement_id: Arca gana di LACMA menampilkan sosok yang memukul genderang berbentuk jam pasir yang diikat pada perutnya yang besar sambil menari mengikuti iramanya.
claims.quote: This gana uses percussion mallets to play an hourglass-shaped drum tied to his ample girth while he dances to its beat.

claims.statement_id: Shiva Purana menyebut Ganesha dinyatakan sebagai pejabat ketua oleh semua, termasuk Brahma, Wisnu, dan Shiva, demi menyenangkan Parvati.
claims.quote: In order to gratify Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa was proclaimed as the presiding officer by all, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and others.

claims.statement: In the Shiva Purana Shiva tells Ganesha to be the presiding officer of all his ganas and worthy of worship.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shiva Purana, Shiva berkata kepada Ganesha agar menjadi pejabat ketua atas semua gananya dan layak dipuja.
claims.quote: Let your name be the most auspicious in the matter of quelling obstacles. Be the presiding officer of all my Gaṇas and worthy of worship now.

claims.statement_id: Shiva Purana menyebut para dewa, para gana, dan bidadari menyanyikan lagu dengan gembira, menari, dan memainkan alat musik.
claims.quote: The gods, the Gaṇas and the celestial damsels sang songs joyously, danced and played on instruments.

claims.statement: According to a study of the Saura Purana quoted by Wisdom Library, the form of Shiva's ganas is like that of Shiva himself: nilakantha, trinetra, with the moon on their heads, wearing tiger skin and decorated with all ornaments.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kajian Saura Purana yang dikutip Wisdom Library, wujud para gana Shiva seperti wujud Shiva sendiri: nilakantha, trinetra, berbulan di kepala, berpakaian kulit harimau, dan dihiasi segala perhiasan.
claims.quote: Gaṇa (गण) refers to the “associates of Śiva” and their form is described in the Saurapurāṇa as follows:—The svarūpa of the Gaṇas of Śiva are like the form of Śiva himself. They are nīlakaṇṭha, trinetra and having moon on their heads, and wearing the skin of tiger, decorated with all the Ornaments.

claims.statement: A Wisdom Library glossary entry says ganas are troops that generally appear in classes, nine classes being mentioned in the Puranas, attached to Shiva and serving under Ganesha, dwelling on Ganaparvata identified with Kailasa.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Wisdom Library menyebut gana sebagai pasukan yang umumnya muncul dalam golongan, sembilan golongan disebut dalam Purana, yang terikat pada Shiva dan berada di bawah komando Ganesha, bermukim di Ganaparvata yang diidentifikasi dengan Kailasa.
claims.quote: Gaṇas are troops who generally appear in classes. Nine such classes are mentioned in the Purāṇas: ... These are attached to Lord Śiva and serve under the command of Gaṇeśa, dwelling on Gaṇaparvata identified with Kailāsa—a peak of the Himālaya mountain.

claims.statement: In the Shiva Purana Shiva's Ganas call themselves "the excellent Ganas of Shiva", his doorkeepers, who have come at Shiva's bidding to throw Ganesha out.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shiva Purana para Gana Siwa menyebut diri "Gana Siwa yang terkemuka", penjaga pintunya, yang datang atas perintah Siwa untuk mengusir Ganesha.
claims.quote: We are the excellent Gaṇas of Śiva. We are his doorkeepers. We have come here to throw you out at the bidding of lord Śiva.

claims.statement: Thousands of Shiva's Ganas flee in all directions like deer on seeing a lion, and Ganesha returns to the doorway and stands there.
claims.statement_id: Ribuan Gana Siwa lari ke segala arah seperti rusa melihat singa, lalu Ganesha kembali ke pintu dan berdiri di sana.
claims.quote: Just as deer flee to any direction on seeing a lion, the Gaṇas, who were thousands in number fled in that manner. Then Gaṇeśa returned to doorway and stood there.

claims.statement: Shiva says the boy at his door has destroyed many of his attendants and forcefully defeated his Ganas.
claims.statement_id: Siwa berkata bahwa anak penjaga pintu itu telah menghancurkan banyak pengiringnya dan mengalahkan para Gananya dengan kekuatan.
claims.quote: He has destroyed many of my Pārṣadas. He has forcefully defeated my Gaṇas.

claims.statement: Shiva issues directives to Indra and other gods, to the Ganas led by the six-faced Kumara, and to goblins, ghosts and spirits; at his bidding they all desire to kill Ganesha.
claims.statement_id: Siwa memerintahkan Indra dan dewa-dewa lain, para Gana yang dipimpin Kumara berwajah enam, serta goblin, hantu, dan roh; atas perintah Siwa mereka semua ingin membunuh Ganesha.
claims.quote: He issued directives to Indra and other gods, to the Gaṇas led by the six-faced Kumāra and to goblins, ghosts and spirits. ... At the bidding of Śiva they all desired to kill Gaṇeśa.

claims.statement: To destroy Daksha's sacrifice Shiva sends crores of valorous Ganas, equal to the fire of dissolution.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menghancurkan yajna Daksha, Siwa mengirim berkoti-koti Gana yang gagah berani, setara dengan api peleburan.
claims.quote: To add lustre to the campaign, Śiva sent crores of Gaṇas, very valorous and equal to the fire of dissolution.

claims.statement: At Shiva's bidding Virabhadra advances followed by crores and crores, thousands and thousands, hundreds and hundreds of Ganas.
claims.statement_id: Atas perintah Siwa, Virabhadra berangkat diikuti berkoti-koti, beribu-ribu, dan beratus-ratus Gana.
claims.quote: Thus at the bidding of Śiva, the heroic Vīrabhadra went ahead followed by crores and crores, thousands and thousands, hundreds and hundreds of Gaṇas.

claims.statement: The guardians of the quarters including Indra fight fiercely with Virabhadra's Ganas; Indra fights Nandin and Kubera fights Kushmandapati.
claims.statement_id: Para penjaga penjuru termasuk Indra bertarung sengit dengan para Gana Virabhadra; Indra melawan Nandin dan Kubera melawan Kushmandapati.
claims.quote: The guardians of the quarters including Indra roared like lions and fought forcefully with the Gaṇas of Vīrabhadra. 6. A noisy terrible fight ensued between the Gaṇas and the guardians of the quarters, both roaring like lions. 7. Indra fought with Nandin; the fire-god with Aśman and the powerful Kubera fought with Kūṣmāṇḍapati.

claims.statement: A great voice makes Vishnu realize that the great Ganas are invincible, and he thinks of vanishing from the scene.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah suara agung menyadarkan Wisnu bahwa para Gana yang agung tak terkalahkan, sehingga ia berpikir untuk menghilang dari medan itu.
claims.quote: Viṣṇu was enlightened by the great voice that the great Gaṇas were invincible. He therefore thought of vanishing from the scene.

claims.statement: Trijata is a Ramayana rakshasi assigned to guard Sita in Lanka.
claims.statement_id: Trijata adalah rakshasi Ramayana yang ditugaskan menjaga Sita di Lanka.
claims.quote: is a rakshasi (demoness) in the Hindu epic Ramayana who is assigned the duty of guarding goddess Sita

claims.statement: In later adaptations she is called Vibhishana's daughter.
claims.statement_id: Dalam adaptasi belakangan ia disebut putri Vibhishana.
claims.quote: Trijata (Sanskrit: त्रिजटा, IAST: Trijaṭā) is a rakshasi (demoness) in the Hindu epic Ramayana who is assigned the duty of guarding goddess Sita who was kidnapped by the demon-king of Lanka Ravana. In later adaptions of Ramayana, Trijata is described as a daughter of Vibhishana, the brother of Ravana.

claims.statement: She is depicted as old and wise and dreams of Ravana's destruction and Rama's victory.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan tua dan bijaksana serta bermimpi tentang kehancuran Ravana dan kemenangan Rama.
claims.quote: Trijata appears as a wise old rakshasi, who dreams of Ravana's destruction and the victory of God Rama,

claims.statement: She generally becomes a loyal friend comforting Sita in adversity.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya ia menjadi sahabat setia yang menghibur Sita dalam kesulitan.
claims.quote: Barring a few exceptions where Trijata is cast as Ravana's agent, she is generally portrayed as a friend and loyal companion of Goddess Sita in Her adversity. On numerous occasions, she offers solace to Goddess Sita and brings news from the outside world; she also dissuades Goddess Sita from committing suicide.

claims.statement: Regional names include Punukay in Laos and Benyakai in Thailand's Ramakien.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dalam versi regional termasuk Punukay di Laos dan Benyakai dalam Ramakien Thailand.
claims.quote: While Indian, Javanese and Balinese versions of the Ramayana call her Trijata, she is known as Punukay in the Laotian Phra Lak Phra Lam, Benyakai (เบญกาย) in the Thai Ramakien and Devi Seri Jali in the Malay Hikayat Seri Rama.

claims.statement: In Griffith's translation Trijata asks the other rakshasis to spare Dasharatha's heir's wife.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Griffith, Trijata meminta rakshasi lain menyelamatkan istri pewaris Dasharatha.

claims.statement: Vetalas are a class of Hindu supernatural beings inhabiting charnel grounds.
claims.statement_id: Vetala adalah golongan makhluk gaib Hindu yang menghuni tempat pembakaran jenazah.
claims.quote: is a class of beings in Hindu mythology. They are usually defined as a knowledgeable (fortune telling) paranormal entity said to be dwelling at charnel grounds.

claims.statement: These spirits use reanimated corpses as vehicles and can possess or leave them.
claims.statement_id: Roh ini menggunakan jasad yang dihidupkan kembali sebagai kendaraan dan dapat masuk atau meninggalkannya.
claims.quote: A vetala (Sanskrit: वेताल, romanized: vetāla) is a class of beings in Hindu mythology. They are usually defined as a knowledgeable (fortune telling) paranormal entity said to be dwelling at charnel grounds. Reanimated corpses are used as vehicles by these spirits for movement. A vetala may possess and leave a dead body at will.

claims.statement: Traditions depict them troubling people but also guarding villages.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi menggambarkannya mengganggu manusia, tetapi juga menjaga desa.
claims.quote: In Hindu folklore, the vetala is an evil spirit who haunts cemeteries and takes demonic possession of corpses. They make their displeasure known by troubling humans. They can drive people mad, kill children, and cause miscarriages, but also guard villages.

claims.statement: Mantras can repel them and funerary rites release them from ghostly existence.
claims.statement_id: Mantra dapat mengusirnya dan upacara pemakaman dapat membebaskannya dari keberadaan sebagai roh.
claims.quote: These creatures can be repelled by the chanting of mantras. One can free them from their ghostly existence by performing their funerary rites.

claims.statement: The Vetala Panchavimshati contains twenty five stories with a vetala and King Vikramaditya as central figures.
claims.statement_id: Vetala Panchavimshati memuat dua puluh lima cerita dengan vetala dan raja Vikramaditya sebagai tokoh utama.
claims.quote: The Vetala Panchavimshati is a collection of twenty-five stories, featuring a vetala as one of the two central characters. It is a part of the Kathasaritsagara, a work that was compiled no later than the 11th century. It features a frame story of a sorcerer who asks King Vikramaditya to capture a corpse hanging on a tree that stands in the middle of a cremation ground.

claims.statement_id: Sharabha adalah makhluk berkaki delapan yang sebagian singa dan sebagian burung dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is an eight-legged part-lion and part-bird deity in Hindu religion,

claims.statement: In Shaiva texts Shiva takes Sharabha's form to pacify Narasimha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks Shaiva, Shiva mengambil wujud Sharabha untuk menenangkan Narasimha.
claims.quote: The Shaiva scriptures narrate that the deity Shiva assumed the form of Sharabha to pacify Narasimha - the fierce man-lion avatar of Vishnu worshipped by the Vaishnava sect. This form is popularly known as Sharabheshvara ("Lord Sharabha") or Sharabheshvaramurti.

claims.statement: Some Vaishnava versions say Gandabherunda defeats Sharabha.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah versi Vaishnava menyebut Gandabherunda mengalahkan Sharabha.
claims.quote: Vishnu assumed the form of the ferocious two-headed bird Gandabherunda, who in turn defeated Sharabha.

claims.statement: In Jataka narratives Sharabha is a former birth of the Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Jataka, Sharabha merupakan kelahiran terdahulu Buddha.
claims.quote: In Buddhism, Sharabha appears in Jataka Tales as an earlier birth of the Buddha. It also appears in Tibetan Buddhist art, symbolizing the perfection of effort. As a figure of power and majesty, Sharabha has appeared in numerous emblems.

claims.statement_id: Tataka adalah tokoh yakshi antagonis dalam Ramayana yang mengganggu ritual para resi bersama Maricha.
claims.quote: Tāṭakā is a minor yakṣī antagonist in the Rāmāyaṇa. Along with her son, Mārīca, Tāṭakā would harass and attack sages performing yajñas in the forest.

claims.statement: Suketu receives Tataka as a daughter with the strength of a thousand elephants.
claims.statement_id: Suketu memperoleh Tataka sebagai putri dengan kekuatan seribu gajah.
claims.quote: In the Rāmāyaṇa, Viśvāmitra tells Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa the story of Tāṭakā when they reach a forest inhabited by her. Viśvāmitra states that a yakṣa named Suketu had undertaken austerities to obtain children, and was given a daughter with the strength of a thousand elephants named Tāṭakā, but not a son. When she became of age, she was married to Sunda, and gave birth to a son named Mārīca.

claims.statement: She marries Sunda and bears Maricha.
claims.statement_id: Ia menikah dengan Sunda dan melahirkan Maricha.

claims.quote: Tāṭakā and Mārīca attack the seer Agastya, who curses Mārīca to become a rākṣasa and curses Tāṭakā to become an ugly man-eater.

claims.statement: Rama kills her with one arrow to the chest under Vishvamitra's direction.
claims.statement_id: Rama membunuhnya dengan satu panah ke dada atas arahan Vishvamitra.
claims.quote: Tāṭakā then charges Rāma, who proceeds to shoot and kill her with a single arrow to the chest.
