claims.statement: Danavas are a class descending from Kashyapa and Danu, Daksha's daughter, in Hindu belief.
claims.statement_id: Danava adalah golongan keturunan Kashyapa dan Danu, putri Daksha, dalam keyakinan Hindu.
claims.quote: In Hindu belief, the danavas are a race descending from Kashyapa and his wife Danu, a daughter of the progenitor god, Daksha. It is mentioned that there are one hundred danavas.

claims.statement: They belong to the asuras and are half brothers of devas and daityas.
claims.statement_id: Mereka merupakan bagian dari asura dan saudara seayah para deva serta daitya.
claims.quote: The danavas are a legendary race of asuras, the half-brothers to the devas and daityas that are found in a range of Hindu texts. The danavas are a part of a larger group of the asuras, and are typically portrayed as opposed to the Hindu deities.

claims.statement: They are usually depicted opposing deities but their relationships and identity boundaries vary within the tradition's history.
claims.statement_id: Mereka biasanya digambarkan melawan dewa, tetapi hubungan dan batas identitasnya beragam dalam sejarah tradisi.
claims.quote: are typically portrayed as opposed to the Hindu deities. However, historically, their role in Hinduism is varied and at times, the distinction between the danavas and Hindu deities is complex and they are difficult to distinguish from one another.

claims.statement: The name Danava comes from their mother Danu's name.
claims.statement_id: Nama Danava berasal dari nama ibu mereka, Danu.
claims.quote: The name danavas stems from the mother's name: Danu.

claims.statement: In the summarized narrative devas exile them from Svarga in the Satya Yuga and they shelter in Vindhya.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah yang diringkas, para deva mengusir mereka dari Svarga pada Satya Yuga dan mereka berlindung di Vindhya.
claims.quote: The devas exiled the danavas from Svarga during the Satya Yuga. After the exile, the danavas are held to have taken refuge in the Vindhya range.

claims.statement: Mackenzie's retelling places Danavas and Daityas in Patala under Varuna's sway.

claims.quote:

there “afflicted by Time”, ... subject to the sway
of Varuna.

claims.statement: Apasmara is a diminutive man symbolizing spiritual ignorance and ahamkara in Hindu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Apasmara adalah manusia kerdil yang melambangkan ketidaktahuan rohani dan ahamkara dalam mitologi Hindu.
claims.quote: Apasmara (Sanskrit: अपस्मार , IAST: Apasmāra) is a diminutive man who represents spiritual ignorance and ahamkara in Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: His other names are Muyalaka or Muyalakan.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya adalah Muyalaka atau Muyalakan.
claims.quote: He is also known as Muyalaka or Muyalakan.

claims.statement: The word apasmara means loss of memory.
claims.statement_id: Kata apasmara berarti kehilangan ingatan.
claims.quote: The compound apasmāra means loss of memory,

claims.statement: In iconography he often holds a cobra symbolizing ahamkara in Shaiva traditions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ikonografi ia sering memegang kobra yang melambangkan ahamkara dalam tradisi Shaiva.
claims.quote: Apasmara, depicted as a diminutive man, is often shown in Hindu iconography clutching a cobra, which symbolizes (ahamkara) in Shaivite tradition.

claims.statement: Nataraja subdues him beneath his right foot during the cosmic dance.
claims.statement_id: Nataraja menundukkannya di bawah kaki kanan dalam tarian kosmis.
claims.quote: During this dance, Shiva subdues Apasmara under his right foot, symbolizing the subjugation of ignorance and ahamkara.

claims.statement: The Cleveland Museum describes the dwarfish figure under Nataraja's steps as personified ignorance.
claims.statement_id: Museum Cleveland menjelaskan sosok kerdil di bawah langkah Nataraja sebagai personifikasi ketidaktahuan.
claims.quote: With every step in his dance, he lands on a dwarfish figure personifying ignorance.

claims.statement: Wikipedia says Apasmara symbolizes the ignorance of selfhood (ahamkara), a universal, cosmic form of ignorance essential for jivas to function in samsara by forgetting past lives and identifying with a new body each time.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menyebut Apasmara melambangkan ketidaktahuan akan jati diri (ahamkara), bentuk ketidaktahuan kosmis yang diperlukan agar jiwa (jiva) berfungsi dalam samsara dengan melupakan kehidupan lampau dan mengidentifikasi diri dengan tubuh baru setiap kali.
claims.quote: Apasmara symbolizes the ignorance of selfhood (ahamkara), a universal, cosmic form of ignorance essential for jivas to function in samsara across their countless rebirths by forgetting past lives and identifying with a new body each time.

claims.statement: To enable moksha (transcendence) while preserving the cosmic balance between spiritual knowledge and the ignorance inherent in samsara, Apasmara must be subdued rather than killed.
claims.statement_id: Agar moksha (transendensi) dimungkinkan sambil menjaga keseimbangan kosmis antara pengetahuan rohani dan ketidaktahuan dalam samsara, Apasmara harus ditundukkan, bukan dibunuh.
claims.quote: To enable moksha (transcendence) while preserving the cosmic balance between spiritual knowledge and ignorance inherent in samsara, Apasmara must be subdued rather than killed.

claims.statement: Apasmara is believed to remain eternally subdued beneath Nataraja's foot, with Shiva perpetually maintaining this balance through his cosmic dance.
claims.statement_id: Apasmara dipercaya tetap tertundukkan selamanya di bawah kaki Nataraja, dengan Shiva terus menjaga keseimbangan itu lewat tarian kosmisnya.
claims.quote: Apasmara is believed to remain eternally subdued beneath Nataraja's foot, with Shiva perpetually maintaining this balance through his cosmic dance.

claims.statement: Similar symbolism appears in representations of Dakshinamurti, another form of Shiva as a guru, where Apasmara is subdued under Shiva's right foot.
claims.statement_id: Simbolisme serupa terlihat pada penggambaran Dakshinamurti, wujud lain Shiva sebagai guru, tempat Apasmara ditundukkan di bawah kaki kanan Shiva.
claims.quote: Similar symbolism is seen in representations of Dakshinamurti, another form of Shiva as a guru, where Apasmara is subdued under Shiva’s right foot.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that Aldous Huxley, in his utopian novel Island, describes Nataraja's right foot planted on a horrible little subhuman creature, the demon Muyalaka.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Aldous Huxley, dalam novel utopianya Island, melukiskan kaki kanan Nataraja bertumpu pada makhluk kecil mengerikan yang kurang dari manusia, iblis Muyalaka.
claims.quote: Aldous Huxley has described and summarized the symbolism of Nataraja and Apasmara, also known as Muyalaka in his utopian novel, Island: Nataraja's right foot is planted squarely on a horrible little subhuman creature - the demon, Muyalaka.

claims.statement: In the novel's passage Muyalaka is a dwarf immensely powerful in his malignity, the embodiment of ignorance and of greedy, possessive selfhood.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan dari novel itu, Muyalaka adalah sosok kerdil yang sangat kuat dalam kejahatannya, perwujudan ketidaktahuan dan diri yang tamak dan posesif.
claims.quote: A dwarf, but immensely powerful in his malignity, Muyalaka is the embodiment of ignorance, the manifestation of greedy, possessive selfhood.

claims.statement: The Cleveland Museum of Art notes that the trampled figure holds a serpent in his left hand and with his right points up to Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Museum Cleveland mencatat bahwa sosok yang diinjak itu memegang ular di tangan kirinya dan dengan tangan kanannya menunjuk ke atas kepada Shiva.
claims.quote: The trampled figure holds a serpent in his left hand and with his right points up to Shiva.

claims.statement: As described in the Kalikakhanda of the Skanda Purana, Apasmara should be black, with three heads and three eyes, six protruding canine teeth, three legs and six hands.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi Apasmara dalam Kalikakhanda dari Skanda Purana, ia seharusnya hitam, berkepala tiga dan bermata tiga, bertaring enam yang menonjol, berkaki tiga, dan bertangan enam.
claims.quote: As per the description of Apasmāra in Kālikākhaṇḍa of Skandapurāṇa, he should be black in color, have three heads and three eyes, six protruding canine teeth, three legs and six hands.

claims.statement: The study notes that, except for the protruding canine teeth, no other feature of that description can be traced in any image of Apasmarapurusha, in sculptures or paintings.
claims.statement_id: Kajian itu mencatat bahwa, kecuali taring yang menonjol, tidak ada ciri lain dari uraian tersebut yang dapat ditemukan pada gambar Apasmarapurusha, baik pada arca maupun lukisan.
claims.quote: Except the protruding canine teeth no other feature can be traced in any of the images of Apasmārapuruṣa either in sculptures or in paintings.

claims.statement: A Wisdom Library glossary describes Apasmarapurusha as epilepsy or loss of memory personified; according to the Skanda Purana he is black with three heads and should be playing with a snake.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Wisdom Library menyebut Apasmarapurusha sebagai epilepsi atau kehilangan ingatan yang dipersonifikasikan; menurut Skanda Purana ia hitam berkepala tiga dan seharusnya bermain dengan ular.
claims.quote: Apasmārapuruṣa (अपस्मारपुरुष) refers to epilepsy, loss of memory personified.—Apasmārapuruṣa, according to Skandapurāṇa is black with three heads etc. (Lakkaṇṇa, Śivatattvacintāmaṇi, p.137 ff). Apasmārapuruṣa should be playing with a snake.

claims.statement: On the Nataraja sculpture at the temple of Lokeshvara, according to a study quoted by Wisdom Library, Apasmara wears a dhoti, his face is lifted up to the left of Shiva, and he has a small horn.
claims.statement_id: Pada arca Nataraja di pura Lokeshvara, menurut kajian yang dikutip Wisdom Library, Apasmara berpakaian dhoti, wajahnya terangkat di sebelah kiri Shiva, dan ia bertanduk kecil.
claims.quote: Apasmāra is clad with a dhotī with kacce clearly traceable. His face is to the left of Śiva, lifted up, and he has a small horn.

claims.statement: In the Thillai legend the sages gathered all their spiritual strength and invoked the powerful demon Muyalakan, a symbol of complete arrogance and ignorance; Shiva stepped on his back to immobilise him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Thillai, para resi mengerahkan seluruh kekuatan rohani mereka dan memanggil iblis perkasa Muyalakan, lambang kesombongan dan ketidaktahuan; Siwa menginjak punggungnya untuk melumpuhkannya.
claims.quote: The sages gathered all their spiritual strength and invoked the powerful demon Muyalakan — a symbol of complete arrogance and ignorance. ... Shiva smiled gently, stepped on the demon's back to immobilise him

claims.statement: After Muyalakan was immobilised, Shiva performed the Ananda Thandavam and disclosed his true form; the sages surrendered, realizing that rituals cannot control the gods.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Muyalakan dilumpuhkan, Siwa menarikan Ananda Thandavam dan menyingkapkan wujud sejatinya; para resi menyerah karena sadar bahwa ritual tidak dapat mengendalikan para dewa.
claims.quote: and performed the Ánanda Thandavam (the dance of eternal bliss), thus disclosing his true form. The sages surrendered, realizing that rituals cannot control the gods.

claims.statement: In the Skanda Purana the sages' black-magic sacrifice produces a serpent, a lion, an elephant (or tiger) and a dwarf that all attack Shiva; Shiva overpowers them, then dances on the dwarf and takes the form of Nataraja, the Cosmic Dancer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Skanda Purana, kurban sihir hitam para resi menghasilkan ular, singa, gajah (atau harimau), dan seorang kerdil yang semuanya menyerang Siwa; Siwa mengalahkan mereka, lalu menari di atas si kerdil dan mengambil wujud Nataraja.
claims.quote: they perform a black magic sacrifice, which produces a serpent, a lion, an elephant (or tiger), and a dwarf, all of which attack Shiva, who overpowers them. ... Shiva then dances on the dwarf and takes the form of Nataraja, the Cosmic Dancer.

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia: Shiva stamps on the dwarf figure Apasmara Purusha, who represents illusion and leads men away from the truth.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia: Siwa menginjak sosok kerdil Apasmara Purusha, yang melambangkan ilusi dan menyesatkan manusia dari kebenaran.
claims.quote: He also stamps one foot on the dwarf figure Apasmara Purusha who represents illusion and who leads men away from the truth.

claims.statement: According to Coomaraswamy, Nataraja's lower left hand points down to the demon Muyalaka, who holds a cobra and is crushed by Shiva's right foot.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Coomaraswamy, tangan kiri bawah Nataraja menunjuk ke iblis Muyalaka yang memegang kobra, dan iblis itu diinjak oleh kaki kanan Siwa.
claims.quote: The upper left hand holds a flame, the lower left hand points down to the demon Muyalaka, who is shown holding a cobra. The demon is being crushed by Shiva’s right foot;

claims.quote: This "necessary evil" of Apasmara is part of the cosmic balance between spiritual knowledge and the inherent ignorance in one's sense of self, and cannot be eradicated without disrupting the cosmic order.

claims.statement_id: Dalam Hindu mereka mengiringi Shiva dan digolongkan sebagai setengah dewa.
claims.quote: In Hinduism, they also attend Shiva, who lives in the Himalayas. They are considered Upadevas, or demi-gods.

claims.statement: Hindu epics depict them as air spirits scattering flowers and rejoicing with music.
claims.statement_id: Epos Hindu menggambarkan mereka sebagai roh udara yang menabur bunga dan bergembira dengan musik.
claims.quote: Vidyādharas are described as essentially spirits of the air. ... strewing flowers watching a combat, rejoicing with music and laughter,

claims.quote: They possess great magical powers like the ability to diminish their size.

claims.statement: Jain narratives describe them as human or semidivine lineages with vidya sciences or powers.
claims.statement_id: Narasi Jain menggambarkan mereka sebagai garis keturunan manusia atau semi-ilahi dengan ilmu atau kekuatan vidya.
claims.quote: Jain narrative texts describe Vidyadharas as human or semi-divine lineages who possess Vidyas, or special sciences and powers. claims.statement: Yali or Vyala is a Hindu creature with a lion body, elephant trunk and tusks, and sometimes equine features.
claims.statement_id: Yali atau Vyala adalah makhluk Hindu dengan tubuh singa, belalai dan gading gajah, kadang unsur kuda.
claims.quote: is a Hindu mythological creature, portrayed with the head and the body of a lion, the trunk and the tusks of an elephant, and sometimes bearing equine features.

claims.statement_id: Figurnya sering dipahat pada pilar kuil India Selatan.
claims.quote: Yali (IAST: Yāḷi, Tamil: யாளி), also called Vyāla (Sanskrit: व्याल), is a Hindu mythological creature, portrayed with the head and the body of a lion, the trunk and the tusks of an elephant, and sometimes bearing equine features. Images of the creature occur in many South Indian temples, often sculpted onto the pillars.

claims.statement: Yalis become prominent in sixteenth century South Indian sculpture.
claims.statement_id: Yali menjadi menonjol dalam patung India Selatan abad keenam belas.
claims.quote: Descriptions of, and references to, yalis are ancient, but they became prominent in South Indian sculptures in the 16th century. Yalis were described to be more powerful than the lion, the tiger, or the elephant. In its iconography, the yali has a cat-like body, but the head of a lion with the tusks of an elephant (gaja), and the tail of a serpent.

claims.statement: Its iconography can include a serpent tail or standing on a makara.
claims.statement_id: Ikonografinya dapat memiliki ekor ular atau berdiri di atas makara.
claims.quote: the tail of a serpent. Sometimes, they have been shown standing on the back of a makara,

claims.statement: It is regarded as a guardian protecting humans physically and spiritually.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipandang sebagai penjaga yang melindungi manusia secara jasmani dan rohani.
claims.quote: The yali is said to be a guardian creature, protecting human beings both physically and spiritually. It is regarded to be a fearless beast, possessing supremacy over the animal world. It is also believed to be the symbolic representation of man's struggle with the elemental forces of nature. It is even depicted in emblem of Karnataka

claims.statement: Denmark's National Museum describes the yali as a mythical being with a lion's body and face and an elephant trunk.
claims.statement_id: Museum Nasional Denmark menggambarkan yali sebagai makhluk mitos bertubuh dan berwajah singa dengan belalai gajah.
claims.quote: The animal generally called Yali is a mythical leo-griff with a lion! s body and face, but will have a trunk like that of an elephant.

claims.statement: Kirtimukha is a fierce face with large fangs and a gaping mouth in Hindu and Buddhist architecture.
claims.statement_id: Kirtimukha adalah wajah ganas bertaring besar dan bermulut menganga dalam arsitektur Hindu dan Buddha.
claims.quote: is the name of a swallowing fierce face with huge fangs, and gaping mouth, very common in the iconography of Hindu temple architecture in South Asia and Southeast Asia, and often also found in Buddhist architecture.

claims.statement: This ornamental motif has a narrative origin in the Skanda Purana and Shiva Purana.
claims.statement_id: Motif hias ini memiliki asal kisah dalam Skanda Purana dan Shiva Purana.
claims.quote: Unlike other Hindu legendary creatures, for example the sea-dwelling makara, the kirtimukha is essentially an ornamental motif in art, which has its origin in a legend from the Skanda Purana and the Shiva Purana.

claims.statement: Mukha means face and kirti means fame or glory.
claims.statement_id: Mukha berarti wajah dan kirti berarti kemasyhuran atau kemuliaan.
claims.quote: The word mukha in Sanskrit refers to the face while kīrti means "fame, glory".  The story of Kirtimukha begins when the asura king Jalandhara, who "by virtue of extraordinary austerities ... accumulated to himself irresistible powers." In a burst of pride, he sent forth his messenger, the Hindu deity Rahu, whose main task is eclipsing the moon, to challenge Shiva. "The challenge ...

claims.statement: Zimmer interprets it as an apotropaic demon mask and guardian of the threshold.
claims.statement_id: Zimmer menafsirkannya sebagai topeng demon penolak bahaya dan penjaga ambang.
claims.quote: The Kirtimukha is often used as a motif surmounting the pinnacle of a temple or the image of a deity, especially in South Indian architecture. As Zimmer writes, "Kirtimukha serves primarily as an apotropaic demon-mask, a gruesome, awe-inspiring guardian of the threshold."

claims.statement: The motif decorates sanctum doorway lintels, often showing only the upper jaw and upper face.
claims.statement_id: Motif ini menghias lintel pintu ruang suci, sering hanya memperlihatkan rahang atas dan bagian atas wajah.
claims.quote: This fierce face with bulging eyes sits also as an embellishment over the lintel of the gate to the inner sanctum in many Hindu temples ... very often only the upper jaw and top of the face is visible

claims.statement: Singapore's NHB calls kirtimukha an auspicious face of glory in South and Southeast Asian Hindu Buddhist temple architecture.
claims.statement_id: NHB Singapura menyebut kirtimukha sebagai wajah kemuliaan yang mujur dalam arsitektur kuil Hindu-Buddha Asia Selatan dan Tenggara.
claims.quote: The kirtimukha or auspicious face of glory is popular icon in South and Southeast Asian Hindu-Buddhist temple architecture.

claims.statement: Gandabherunda is Vishnu's double headed eagle form in Hindu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Gandabherunda adalah wujud Vishnu sebagai elang berkepala dua dalam mitologi Hindu.
claims.quote: is a form of Vishnu in Hindu mythology. ... assumes this form of a double-headed eagle

claims.statement: In the legend Narasimha takes this form to subdue Sharabha, Shiva's form.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda, Narasimha mengambil wujud ini untuk menundukkan Sharabha, wujud Shiva.
claims.quote: According to legend, Narasimha, an avatar of Vishnu, assumes this form of a double-headed eagle to subdue Sharabha, a form of Shiva.

claims.statement: He is worshipped with Narasimhi, a fierce form of Lakshmi.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipuja bersama Narasimhi, wujud ganas Lakshmi.
claims.quote: Gandabherunda is worshipped along with his consort Narasimhi, a fierce form of Lakshmi, also revered as Simhamukhi Lakshmi.

claims.statement: Depictions show him holding elephants in claws and beaks to reveal his power.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya memegang gajah dengan cakar dan paruh untuk menunjukkan kekuatannya.
claims.quote: The two headed eagle is holding two elephants in his claws and beaks, revealing his enormous powers.

claims.statement: His figure is carved at Belur's Chennakeshava Temple in a chain of cosmic destruction.
claims.statement_id: Figurnya dipahat di kuil Chennakeshava di Belur dalam rangkaian kehancuran kosmis.
claims.quote: In the Chennakeshava Temple, Beluru, Karnataka, Gandabherunda as a two headed eagle is carved in a scene of chain of destruction, which results in the destruction of the universe.

claims.statement: The NHB documents Gandabherunda on a Karnataka braid ornament and calls it the Wodeyar rulers' royal insignia.
claims.statement_id: NHB mendokumentasikan Gandabherunda pada hiasan kepang Karnataka dan menyebutnya lambang kerajaan para penguasa Wodeyar.
claims.quote: the Gandabherunda, a mythic double headed bird, the royal insignia of the Wodeyar rulers (1399 -1947) of Mysore.

claims.statement: On a coin found in Madurai, he is shown holding a snake in his beak.
claims.statement_id: Pada sebuah koin yang ditemukan di Madurai, ia digambarkan memegang ular dengan paruhnya.
claims.quote: In a coin found in Madurai, he is holding a snake in his beak.

claims.statement: All 2-dimensional depictions show a symmetrical image of a double-headed eagle, while other images show his long tail feathers like a peafowl.
claims.statement_id: Semua penggambaran dua dimensi menampilkan citra simetris sebagai elang berkepala dua, sedangkan gambar lain menunjukkan bulu ekor panjangnya seperti merak.
claims.quote: All 2-dimensional depictions show a symmetrical image in which he is a double-headed eagle while other images show his long tail feathers like a peafowl.

claims.statement: In the story Wikipedia records, Vishnu took the form of Gandabherunda as an alternative form of Narasimha, a two-headed eagle animal, and Shiva took the form of Sharabha, a part-lion and part-eagle animal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Wikipedia, Vishnu mengambil wujud Gandabherunda sebagai wujud lain Narasimha, hewan elang berkepala dua, dan Shiva mengambil wujud Sharabha, hewan setengah singa setengah elang.
claims.quote: Vishnu took the form of Gandabherunda as an alternative form of Narasimha, a two-headed eagle animal, and Shiva took the form of Sharabha, a part-lion and part-eagle animal.

claims.statement: In that story the battle between Narasimha as Gandabherunda and Sharabha and Hiranyakashipu lasted 18 days; on the 18th day he disemboweled and killed both Sharabha and Hiranyakashipu at the same time.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, pertempuran Narasimha sebagai Gandabherunda melawan Sharabha dan Hiranyakashipu berlangsung 18 hari; pada hari ke-18 ia membelah perut dan membunuh Sharabha dan Hiranyakashipu sekaligus.
claims.quote: Narasimha as Gandabherunda with Sharabha and Hiranyakashipu fought an 18-day battle. On the 18th day, Narasimha as Gandabherunda disemboweled and killed both Sharabha and Hiranyakashipu at the same time.

claims.statement: As a mark of respect, Sharabha removed the skin of his body and gave it to Narasimha as Gandabherunda, who wore it as a hide and gave it back to Sharabha, who attached it to his body and grew it back fully as his skin.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai tanda hormat, Sharabha menanggalkan kulit tubuhnya dan memberikannya kepada Narasimha sebagai Gandabherunda, yang mengenakannya sebagai kulit lalu memberikannya kembali kepada Sharabha, yang menempelkannya hingga tumbuh penuh sebagai kulitnya lagi.
claims.quote: As a mark of respect, Sharabha removed the skin of his body and gave it to Narasimha as Gandabherunda and Narasimha as Gandabherunda wore it as a hide and gave the hide to Sharabha, who attached the hide to his body and grew it as his skin back fully.

claims.statement: Gandabherunda is used by the Kingdom of Mysore as a royal emblem of the Wodeyar rulers under the Vijayanagaram Empire.
claims.statement_id: Gandabherunda dipakai Kerajaan Mysore sebagai lambang kerajaan para penguasa Wodeyar di bawah Kekaisaran Vijayanagaram.
claims.quote: Gandabherunda is used by the Kingdom of Mysore as a royal emblem of Wodeyar rulers under Vijayanagaram Empire.

claims.statement: The Government of Karnataka has Gandabherunda as a state symbol, found on bus terminals and tickets issued by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation.
claims.statement_id: Pemerintah Karnataka memakai Gandabherunda sebagai lambang negara bagian, dan lambang itu terlihat pada terminal bus dan tiket yang diterbitkan Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation.
claims.quote: Government of Karnataka has Gandabherunda as a state symbol and is found on bus terminals and tickets issued by Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation.

claims.statement: A Wisdom Library glossary (Hindupedia entry) says Gandabherunda, a double-headed eagle, has been the state symbol of many royal dynasties, especially in South India; archaeologists and historians say the bird signifies peace, progress and power.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Wisdom Library (entri Hindupedia) menyebut Gandabherunda, elang berkepala dua, telah menjadi lambang negara banyak dinasti kerajaan, terutama di India Selatan; menurut arkeolog dan sejarawan burung ini menandakan perdamaian, kemajuan, dan kekuasaan.
claims.quote: The Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa (गण्डभेरुण्ड), a double-headed eagle, has been the State symbol of many royal dynasties especially in South India. According to the archaeologists and historians, the bird signifies peace, progress and power.

claims.statement: The Wisdom Library glossary says the Puranas indicate that Vishnu as Gandabherunda subdued Shiva as Sharabha after Narasimha was conquered by Sharabha.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Wisdom Library menyebut Purana menunjukkan bahwa Vishnu sebagai Gandabherunda menundukkan Shiva sebagai Sharabha setelah Narasimha dikalahkan oleh Sharabha.
claims.quote: The Purāṇas indicate that Viṣṇu as Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa subdued Śiva as Śarabha after Narasiṃha was conquered by Śarabha.

claims.statement: A Kannada-English dictionary entry on Wisdom Library defines the word as a fabulous, mythical bird with two heads, believed to be stronger than lions and elephants, a griffin-like bird.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kamus Kannada-Inggris dalam Wisdom Library memerikan kata itu sebagai burung dongeng dan mitos berkepala dua yang dipercaya lebih kuat daripada singa dan gajah, burung mirip griffin.
claims.quote: [noun] a fabulous, mythical bird having two heads, believed to be stronger than lions and elephants; a griffin-like bird.

claims.statement: The same article relates that Narasimha first disemboweled and killed the asura king Hiranyakashipu, then burned and killed all the other asuras and won over them.
claims.statement_id: Artikel yang sama mengisahkan bahwa Narasimha lebih dulu membelah perut dan membunuh raja asura Hiranyakashipu, lalu membakar dan membunuh semua asura lain dan menaklukkan mereka.
claims.quote: After Narasimha disemboweled and killed the asura king Hiranyakashipu, he burned and killed all other asuras and won over them.

claims.statement: Kaliya is a venomous naga in the Yamuna at Vrindavan in Hindu traditions.
claims.statement_id: Kaliya adalah naga beracun dalam sungai Yamuna di Vrindavan menurut tradisi Hindu.
claims.quote: Kaliya (IAST: Kāliya, Devanagari: कालिय), in Hindu traditions,  was a venomous Nāga living in the Yamunā river, in Vṛndāvana. The water of the Yamunā for four leagues all around him boiled and bubbled with poison. No bird or beast could go near, and only one solitary Kadamba tree grew on the river bank.

claims.statement: The surrounding river water is described as boiling and bubbling with poison.
claims.statement_id: Air sungai di sekitarnya digambarkan mendidih dan berbuih karena racun.
claims.quote: Kaliya (IAST: Kāliya, Devanagari: कालिय), in Hindu traditions,  was a venomous Nāga living in the Yamunā river, in Vṛndāvana. The water of the Yamunā for four leagues all around him boiled and bubbled with poison. No bird or beast could go near, and only one solitary Kadamba tree grew on the river bank.

claims.statement: The Krishna and Kaliya account appears in Bhagavata Purana canto ten chapter sixteen.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Krishna dan Kaliya terdapat dalam Bhagavata Purana canto sepuluh bab enam belas.
claims.quote: The incident of Krishna and Kāliya is told in the sixteenth chapter of the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavata Purana.

claims.statement: He leaves his Ramanaka homeland in fear of Garuda.
claims.statement_id: Ia meninggalkan tempat asalnya di Ramanaka karena takut pada Garuda.
claims.quote: The proper home of Kāliya was the island of Ramaṇaka, but he had been driven away from there in fear of Garuḍa, the foe of all serpents. Garuḍa had been cursed by the yogi Saubhari dwelling at Vrindavan so that he could not come to Vrindavan without meeting his death. Therefore, Kāliya chose Vrindavan as his residence, knowing it was the only place where Garuḍa could not come.

claims.statement: Krishna dances on Kaliya's heads to release his poison so he no longer pollutes the Yamuna.
claims.statement_id: Krishna menari di atas kepala Kaliya untuk mengeluarkan racunnya sehingga tidak lagi mencemari Yamuna.
claims.quote: Krishna immediately regained his original form and began to jump on all of Kāliya's heads so as to release the poison in the snake so that he could no longer pollute the Yamunā.

claims.statement: In the Vedabase Bhagavata version Krishna orders Kaliya to leave the river with his family and return to Ramanaka.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavata versi Vedabase, Krishna memerintahkan Kaliya meninggalkan sungai bersama keluarga dan kembali ke Ramanaka.
claims.quote: Kṛṣṇa told him to leave the Yamunā lake with his family and return to Ramaṇaka Island.

claims.statement: With his boisterous dancing Krishna trampled the serpent's one thousand hoods until his body slackened; vomiting blood from his mouths, Kaliya finally understood that Krishna was the primeval personality, Narayana.
claims.statement_id: Dengan tarian yang riuh Krishna menginjak seribu tudung sang ular sampai tubuhnya lemas; sambil memuntahkan darah dari mulut-mulutnya, Kaliya akhirnya sadar bahwa Krishna adalah pribadi purba, Narayana.
claims.quote: By this wonderful, boisterous dancing, Śrī Kṛṣṇa trampled the serpent’s one thousand hoods until his body slackened. Vomiting blood from his mouths, Kāliya finally understood that Kṛṣṇa was the primeval personality, Lord Nārāyaṇa, the spiritual master of all

claims.statement: Kaliya's wives came and prayed to Krishna with joined palms for mercy for their husband; Kaliya recognized Krishna's greatness and surrendered, promising never to harass anyone again.
claims.statement_id: Istri-istri Kaliya datang berdoa kepada Krishna dengan tangan terkatup memohon belas kasihan bagi suami mereka; Kaliya mengakui keagungan Krishna dan menyerah, berjanji tidak akan mengganggu siapa pun lagi.
claims.quote: But then Kāliya's wives came and prayed to Krishna with joined palms, worshiping him and praying for mercy for their husband. Kāliya recognized the greatness of Krishna and surrendered, promising he would not harass anybody again.
